items.article_title: Nodal signaling establishes a competency window for stochastic cell fate switching
items.note: The quote (the 2022 article's own abstract conclusion; its title states the same finding) describes a stochastic fate switch inside a competence window, which speaks to the question's 'only some cells become endoderm'. One study's conclusion is labelled settled; whether the field treats it so is not in the quote, and the question as a whole (how the pattern becomes fates) is wider.

items.article_title: Knockout of thyroid hormone receptor alpha a (thraa) enhances cardiac regeneration in zebrafish through metabolic and hypoxic regulation
items.note: The quote asserts that elevated thyroid hormone and metabolism promote cardiomyocyte cycle exit and polyploidization, limiting regeneration. The cited 2025 article is a single zebrafish knockout study (title); the quote does not show that it settles the mammal-versus-zebrafish difference the question asks about.

items.article_title: Impaired fin regeneration and angiogenesis in aged zebrafish and turquoise killifish
items.note: The quote supports reduced regeneration with age, in 'both species'; the article title shows these are zebrafish and turquoise killifish, so the zebrafish age facet is supported by one 2023 study. The repeated-amputation part and 'under what conditions' of the question are not addressed by the quote.

items.locator: Announcing the Rule 30 Prizes > The Rule 30 Prize Problems > Problem 1: Does the center column always remain non-periodic?
items.note: The quote states that periodicity is unproven beyond the first billion steps and that a proof is needed. It matches the question. This is a mathematics prize problem on a blog announcement, sitting in a biology register; its attestation is not biology literature.

items.article_title: Zebrafish Vascular Mural Cell Biology: Recent Advances, Development, and Functions
items.locator: 3. Mural Cell Development in Zebrafish > 3.1. Overview of Mural Cell Development during the Early Developmental Stages in Zebrafish
items.note: The quote supports the second half of the question (how and when veins acquire mural coverage is little known, in a 2021 review). The first half, what restricts recruitment to arteries, is not in the quote.

items.article_title: Control of organ size: development, regeneration, and the role of theory in biology
items.note: A 2015 commentary says how organ sizes stay proportionate 'remains mysterious'. It matches the question; it is an opinion in a perspective piece, as of 2015.

items.article_title: Spatiotemporal control of pattern formation during somitogenesis
items.locator: INTRODUCTION > FUTURE DIRECTIONS > The decoding and execution of spatiotemporal information
items.note: The quote says reconstruction of the gene regulatory network executing somite segmentation in the anterior presomitic mesoderm is 'not completely resolved' (2024 review). The named Tbx6, Mesp and Ripply network and the clock-to-boundary step are not in the quote, so it supports a nearby open area more than this specific question.

items.article_title: From Stripes to a Beating Heart: Early Cardiac Development in Zebrafish
items.note: The quote states that it is unclear to what extent arterial and venous pole derivatives share a common progenitor pool in the early lateral plate mesoderm (2021 review). This closely matches the question.

items.article_title: The Physical Basis of Coordinated Tissue Spreading in Zebrafish Gastrulation
items.note: The quote says the mechanisms of radial intercalation are 'not yet fully understood' and itself cites a 2010 review, inside a 2017 article, so the openness statement is dated to the 2010 literature. The question's second part (how much is a response to enveloping-layer expansion) is not in the quote.

items.article_title: Molecular Dating of the Teleost Whole Genome Duplication (3R) Is Compatible With the Expectations of Delayed Rediploidization
items.note: The quote says the dating results remain compatible with a prolonged rediploidization process, which 'remains a viable mechanism' for teleost novelties (the 2024 article's title also says its dating is 'compatible with' delayed rediploidization). That is a statement of compatibility, not a statement that the causal question is unresolved, so a stance of 'open' is not supported by this quote.

items.article_title: Mechanical Stretch and PI3K Signaling Link Cell Migration and Proliferation to Coordinate Epithelial Tubule Morphogenesis in the Zebrafish Pronephros
items.note: The quote says the precise mechanism linking cell stretch to proliferation 'is not known' (2012 article). It matches the question; the openness is as of 2012 and later work was not checked.

items.article_title: Combined mutations of hoxa13a, hoxa13b, and hoxd13a lead to structural shifts in zebrafish soft fin rays providing insight into spiny ray evolution
items.note: The quote says how spines arose, and why fin ray structure differs in some species, 'remains to be fully understood' (2026 article). It matches the question.

items.article_title: Caudal fin shape imprinted during late zebrafish embryogenesis is re-patterned by the Sonic hedgehog pathway

epithelial-repair.title: Epithelial repair patch
epithelial-repair.mission: Ask one question about a cultured epithelial sheet: how do cell-level motility and mechanics set the closure of a gap, and what barrier geometry results? A bounded proposal. Two published mechanics models define what is known. The Morpheus engine run here is named as a possible instrument. No wound simulation exists in this node yet.
limitations: Every member ref is a snapshot-catalog ref (namespace 'snapshot'), not a live-store version: re-pin before submitting.
The cited papers have no record in the catalog, so they are not members. They appear as sources on the page, read at abstract level only.
No calibration bridges any pair of scales; every coupling is absent or scenario-level.
No runner exists for this project; every instrument is proposed. Nothing here is a simulation or an observation.

scale_coverage.note: Protrusion and contractility are inputs of the published models; none is modelled here.
Two abstracts describe cell mechanics and adhesion; no parameter is sourced here.
Two published models of closure are known at abstract level; none has been run here.

requirements.text: In a declared stress-free, force-balanced model with no other active drive, setting protrusion intensity to zero leaves closed area constant to numerical tolerance. Falsified if: Closure anyway triggers diagnosis, not a presumed defect: passive relaxation, initial stress, cell-cell or cell-substrate forces or another active mechanism can legitimately close a gap. No mechanism is read from the run until the cause is found.

Closure efficiency changes with initial gap size and with protrusion intensity, as Bai and Zeng report. The abstract gives no direction, so none is assumed. Falsified if: A run that shows no dependence on either does not reproduce the reported dependence.

Paired runs from the same initial state give closed area within tolerance when dt (and grid, where there is one) is refined. Cell count is also preserved only under a declared no-birth, no-death assumption. Seed-to-seed variability is reported as an ensemble spread, not tested for equality. Falsified if: A paired change larger than the tolerance voids the comparison for that setup. Variation across independent seeds is not by itself a defect.
This project is not a clinical treatment or wound-care claim; not a viable engineered organism; not observed wound healing in any fish tissue; not evidence for fin regeneration.

open_questions.text: What evidence would connect a lower-scale prediction to tissue-scale closure in one named cell line? (The same shape of gap as the registered question F002.)
Is closure efficiency against gap size comparable between a Cellular Potts and a continuum model once both are calibrated to one measurement?
What barrier-geometry readout (remaining gap shape) is worth measuring beyond closed area?

flying-fish.title: Engineer toward a flying fish
flying-fish.mission: Engineer toward a flying fish: explore, with typed models and refusals, what a flying-fish-like glider would require. This is a design-studio project on a generic schema; it does not assert that any design is feasible.
limitations: Every member ref is a snapshot-catalog ref (namespace 'snapshot'), not a live-store version: re-pin before submitting.
Membership is a declared pin and states where a record applies; it infers no causal link between members.
No calibration bridges any pair of scales; every coupling above the organ scale is refused or assumption-level.
The numeric requirements are Fish 1990 observed ranges proposed as a design envelope, not a feasibility certificate.

scale_coverage.note: One molecule-to-fin source (Daane 2021, association in zebrafish); no executable model, no parameter link to wing area.
No structure or affinity input for a fin-patterning protein; the one binding test was stopped at its coverage floor.
A two-cell Delta-Notch model is replayed in this project but it is non-dimensional and not tied to a fish; no cell-to-fin coupling exists.

Darwin 1859, a phylogeny and a fossil source as context; no ecological model.

What is the effective flexural rigidity of an excised fin ray under the clamping that matches its in-fin boundary condition? The beam model sweeps an assumed range.
Is there a sourced upper size limit for a gliding fish? Davenport 2003, the paper that argues one, is unread.

tissue-microcarrier.title: Contractile tissue microcarrier
tissue-microcarrier.mission: Ask one question about a Xenopus-inspired contractile tissue construct: how does a chosen actuation pattern turn into deformation, and how much of that deformation becomes net motion? A bounded proposal. A generic soft-body mechanics runner and existing cell-scale tools are named as instruments. No simulation of this construct exists in this node yet, and no frog or fish parameter is used.

requirements.text: With actuation off, from zero initial velocity and a settled force-balanced shape, with no external flow or forcing, a defined reference frame and after a stated transient window, net displacement is zero to numerical tolerance. Falsified if: A nonzero passive displacement under those stated conditions triggers diagnosis of the setup or the runner. If a condition was not met, the control is restated, not read as a defect. No other endpoint is read until it is resolved.

Two predeclared patterns with equal total actuation give net displacements that differ by more than a dt or mesh refinement changes either one. Falsified if: If the difference is smaller than the refinement change, no pattern-to-motion statement is made.
A mirrored pattern on a symmetric body gives the mirrored displacement. Falsified if: A failure marks an anisotropy artifact in the body or the solver.
This project is not a designed living organism or a release claim; not a clinical or medical claim; not a fish tissue, or part of the flying-fish design; not frog-validated mechanics.

why_this_one: It is the only item that both removes an explicit essential blocker (tissue-to-EI) and has a stated measurement in the owning handoff.

design_review.note: Source-only review prompts written from this repository's own project projection and model-coupling report. They are not challenges by reviewers, not new findings and not biological observations. Replace them with Project records and real annotations when the node serves them.
design_review.meaning: A design review is an authored, falsifiable challenge attached to one exact Project version. It is not a vote, consensus score, answer, scientific adjudication or project resolution. A reply does not change the challenged Project.

source_prompts.title: Fin-beam load bridge is scenario-level
source_prompts.observation: The organ panel calls the fin-beam model a scoped elastic surrogate. docs/model-coupling.md marks the load-to-beam bridge scenario-level: mean lift-pressure proxy times a declared tributary width, a declared ray-length fraction and an assumed EI. There is no calibrated fin stiffness or measured ray pressure.
source_prompts.ask: Which loading regime and measured stiffness would falsify this bridge?

source_prompts.title: Notch/Delta to fin stiffness is refused
source_prompts.observation: The coupling report refuses the Collier Notch/Delta to fin-stiffness bridge: there is no mapping, and the transfer spans cell-to-organ and taxon contexts.
source_prompts.ask: What exact, context-matched developmental or tissue measurement would be required before this counts as a biological bridge?

source_prompts.title: Zebrafish interaction phenocopies fin proportion; transfer to halfbeaks unestablished
source_prompts.observation: The Daane 2021 zebrafish interaction phenocopies flying-fish fin proportion, but transfer to halfbeaks is unestablished and no developmental model connects adult proportions to a program.
source_prompts.ask: Which test separates correlation from the asserted genotype-to-fin pathway, with exact source and model pins?

source_prompts.title: Glide release convention drives much of the range
source_prompts.observation: The glide report uses a release at 1.5 times stall speed from 1 m, equivalent to release heights from about 1.8 m to 32.6 m. It says this convention drives much of the range and is a model artifact.
source_prompts.ask: Compare a sourced fixed-speed or fixed-height release; what observable would reject either?

general_prompts.text: Identify which measured animal, life stage and loading regime justify the modeled fin stiffness; if none is pinned, say unknown and propose a test.
Challenge a ray-to-fin mapping at a specific Project member and cite an exact mesh or source record; say whether the geometry is measured, reconstructed or illustrative.
Separate a level-flight lift constraint from glide and sink predictions; name the regime and the evidence that would falsify the proxy.
Require an exact developmental or genetic Evidence pin before treating a morphology correlation as a causal genotype-to-fin link.
State print material, orientation, minimum feature size and a physical test that could reject the design claim.

examples.passage:
[Wikipedia, Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, wikitext]
Euler–Bernoulli beam theory is limited to small deflections of a [[beam (structure)|beam]] that is subjected to lateral loads only, causing [[Elasticity (physics)|elastic]] bending.
| colspan="2" | '''Cantilever beam with end load'''
| rowspan="4" |[[File:CantBeamPointLoad.svg|350px]]
|-
| <math>M(x) = P(L-x)</math>
| <math>M_A = PL</math>
|-
| <math>Q(x) = P </math>
| <math>Q_{\mathrm{max}} = P</math>
|-
| <math>w(x) = \tfrac{Px^2(3L-x)}{6EI} </math>
| <math>w_C = \tfrac{PL^3}{3EI}</math>

[Alben, Madden & Lauder 2007, PMC2359861, Section 3 text]
In our experiment, we have found using three-point bending tests that the ‘composite’ Young's modulus corresponding to the whole structure is E ≈10 8 –10 9 N m −2 , with the average area moment of inertia I ≈10 −6 cm 4 . Hence, the measured B = EI ≈10 −6 –10 −5 J m.

The product of the lower bounds of E and I (10^8 * 10^-14 = 10^-6) matches the lower bound of B, but the upper bound of B (10^-5) is not reached unless I or E varies further.

claim.text: Loss of oca2 exon 21 in Molino cavefish explains their albinism.

[Warren et al. 2021, Nat Commun, PMC7933363, Results (Europe PMC full-text XML, tags stripped)]
Consistent with the laboratory strains, exon 21 of oca2 is absent in all Molino cavefish samples ( n = 9, Supplementary Fig. 8 ).
We further functionally verified that a change in the oca2 locus is responsible for albinism in the F 2 hybrids, by crossing an albino surface/Pachón F 2 hybrid with a genetically engineered surface fish heterozygous for a deletion in oca2 exon 21 27 . We found that 46.5% of the offspring completely lacked pigment ( n = 40/86, Supplementary Fig. 5j ). This confirms that a change in the oca2 locus is responsible for loss of pigment in the mapping population.

limitations: Print preparation is unvalidated: printer and resin are unknown; nothing has been sliced, loaded into PreForm or printed.

Wall rules are provisional, configurable prop choices (1.0 mm; 1.5 mm for the reinforced prop), checked on sampled faces only (3,000 plus 12,000 samples, or every face of a mesh with fewer faces); a thinner region between samples can be missed.
Membranes and rays are thickened for printing; they are not biological thickness. Flow and fin-ray work use the 1:1 candidate files, not these props.

The -scales file adds 0.2-0.4 mm scale and gill-cover relief: texture below the wall rule by design, not gated by it; whether it resolves depends on the unknown printer. The smooth file is the gated one.
Closed, oriented, single-piece manifold, positive volume and box fit are checked on every file; global self-intersection is not checked.
Engineered illustrative forms: not organisms and not a living or bio-printed construct.
Masses are calculated from mesh volume at the Alpha Grey V1 card density (1220 kg/m3, cured); the prop resin is not chosen and nothing was weighed.
Minimum wall 1.0 mm is a provisional, configurable prop choice, checked on sampled faces only; a thinner region between samples can be missed.

data.grounding_note: A law listed for a file says how the file relates to it (governing, checked, inspired_only, not_applicable); it is not evidence that the printed shape satisfies the law. Masses are calculated from mesh volume times a card density and were not weighed. No part has been printed, weighed, glided or thrown; no launch is cleared; the lift, drag, stability, beam and catch numbers are hand models or simulated scenarios with assumed coefficients (C_L in particular depends on geometry and flow and generally comes from experiment). Failed thresholds are reported as failed. Frozen revisions are read, never edited; inconsistencies in their prose are listed under findings, not corrected.

relation.governing: the law computed a number reported for these bytes (the computation is in the evidence)
relation.checked: a stated check against this law or rule was executed on these bytes; its outcome is in checks[]
relation.inspired_only: the law or source shaped the design; nothing here checks these bytes against it
relation.not_applicable: the law does not apply to this file; the detail says why

check_status.pass: executed on these bytes and met its stated threshold
check_status.fail: executed and did not meet its threshold (never relaxed)
check_status.unresolved: executed, with a reading or reviewer finding that the threshold does not settle
check_status.unknown: not determinable from these bytes (for example the resin is not chosen)
check_status.not_applicable: does not apply; the detail says why
check_status.withdrawn: the file is not to be printed; the detail says why

findings.detail: Every _R print STL of r1-r3 holds the left part (det -1 export pose). Kept byte for byte; fixed in r4-daane-printfix. Fish-frame mass properties, GLBs and flight models were not affected.

Reviewer claude-13: readings down to 0.097 mm (0.115 mm twice on r3) at the x 20 slot's lateral openings, judged feather edges rather than a thin wall; they can print rough, chip, or cut the band. The builder's sampler classed its own 0.31 mm reading there as edge-limited and did not gate it. r1's body has a reviewer reading of 0.317 mm aft of its catch slot, also edge-limited.

biological_constraints.kept reads 'v3a outline, ray count, ray roots, angles and lengths, fin positions and dihedral', but source_candidate is fish3d-v3c-daane-length. The outline_check itself compared against the v3c candidate's own rays.json (builder code), so the check result refers to v3c; the prose string is stale. The frozen manifests are not edited; a later revision will derive the string from the candidate.
findings.source: engineering/glider/build.py (the 'kept' string is a literal; outline_check reads artifacts/fish3d/<candidate>/rays.json)

findings.detail: The frozen ASSEMBLY.md cites a 44-60 mm CG window and lists a 60 mm ballast row. That window came from v3a's planform. For r3/r4 claude-07's constraint is CG x 49.5-55.2 mm, target 52.4, never aft of 54.1 mm before the VLM NP, so the 56 and 60 mm rows are outside it.

The frozen 10.5 g threshold was derived on v3a's 52.9 cm2 paired area. It is retained as a legacy threshold; each assembly also carries its own area-specific cap, recomputed here. Every revision fails both.

cuts.title: Lean for biology · one-minute science cut
Lean for biology · two-minute science cut

limits: Computational prototype; not a biologically realized flying fish.
Simulation playback retains source timing; short clips hold on their final saved state for display only.

claim_reuse.readme:
# Actual Claim reuse through two leased computations

One existing exact public Claim was consumed before two distinct bounded
computations, with actual MCP proposals, coordinator readiness, leases, running
states, proposed Evidence and submitted Actions. Independent review is pending;
the producer has not accepted any record. This demonstrates scoped input reuse
and a contribution workflow, not collective benefit or calibrated fish biology.

The shared [Claim read](claim-read.json) pins
`node-a/Claim/eng-finmech-claim-ei-crit@4998ef85bd98ec64c0f4bc86e77337ea25df7ff5683ac6b62dc9095cf5f62f57`.
Its exact rational stiffness threshold is parsed at runtime and multiplied by the
predeclared margin to construct the solver's actual EI input. There is no fallback
hardcoded candidate stiffness. [Protocol](protocol.json) was committed in
`be4dfc6` before candidate solver runs. The current producer result file differs
from the Claim's named source: the [historical result](source-result.json) was
retrieved from the exact source commit and matches its digest; the
[request](source-request.json) matches the original canonical input hash.

| Distinct candidate | Consumed EI (N m²) | Computed tip/span | Maximum slope (rad) | Declared linear-model domain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Below threshold, 9/10 × Claim threshold | 11907/20480000 | 0.111111111158 | 0.148148148207 | Invalid; retained counterexample |
| Above threshold, 11/10 × Claim threshold | 14553/20480000 | 0.090909090883 | 0.121212121180 | Inside declared limits |

The declared limits are tip/span≤0.1 and slope≤0.2 rad. Both runs passed the frozen
quadrature, zero-load, wrong-law mutation, FEM/analytic and grid/profile checks.
Maximum FEM tip relative errors were 4.22e-10 and 2.88e-10 against the fixed 1e-6
limit. Static FEM used 16, 32 and 64 elements; there is no time step. Actual
compute/control wall times were approximately 0.486 and 0.459 seconds, excluding
MCP transport and preparation. No cloud or GPU job was used.

![Actual saved profiles](candidate-profiles.png)

The existing load bridge and beam solver were reused. All pressure, geometry,
material and validity inputs remain declared illustration assumptions. The
invalid lower candidate is not a biological deformation prediction. Empirical
validation and biological success remain unknown; no success probability,
time/cost saving or agency advantage is assigned.

## Inspectable evidence

- [Audit](audit.json) verifies exact Record digests, producer links, artifact
  bytes, code/protocol pins and chronological Claim-read→input-binding→solver→
  Evidence ordering. It counts two distinct current Action **ids**, not merely
  repeated versions. Its chronology uses producer-witnessed UTC, not an external
  time anchor.
- [Typed uses edges](reuse-verification.json) were read back from the live MCP
  neighborhood; the graph was not truncated. [Public catalog readback](public-catalog-readback.json)
  independently returns both current Action heads as submitted.
- Per-case [lower result](below-threshold/result.json) and
  [higher result](above-threshold/result.json), effective inputs, actual profile
  CSVs, exact pre-run Claim reads, proposed Evidence receipts and submitted Action
  readbacks retain the numerical and workflow details.
- [Execution plan](execution-plan.json), [code pins](code-pin.json),
  [environment](environment.json) and safe MCP transcripts preserve provenance.
  Credentials and lease capabilities are excluded/redacted.
- [Superseded proposals](superseded-proposals.json) preserve one correction made
  **before any lease or computation**: initial ready versions were replaced to
  strengthen protocol/numerics/code cache identity. Scientific inputs and criteria
  were unchanged. Those original versions had no lease and are non-executable
  non-heads; they are excluded from the executed reuse count. Root's original
  coordinator-readiness receipt was not altered.
- [Plot provenance](report-provenance.json) is separate from solver production.
  The figure was rendered from actual saved CSV states. Artifact declarations use
  reference-only content URNs and unknown licenses remain null; public hosting and
  byte-availability projection are separate from scientific acceptance.

The worker used only contributor authority. Readiness came from the coordinator;
review requires a separate operator. At captured producer readback both Actions
were **submitted** and both Evidence records **proposed**. A subsequent reviewer
receipt may update those states without changing these historical receipts.

## Bounded independent replay

Use an isolated checkout and separate output directory. Under a 1-CPU, 4-GiB,
swap-zero, 128-task, 600-second systemd scope with numeric-library threads set to
one, load the frozen protocol and each saved pre-run Claim record, then call
`engineering.claim_reuse.compute.compute(record, protocol, case, review_output)`.
This needs NumPy/SciPy and the existing source tree, not the producer credential.
Check original artifact hashes first; compare physical profiles/metrics under the
already frozen tolerances. Timestamps/wall time make whole-result JSON byte
identity inappropriate. Running the contribution client again is deliberately
blocked by its existing-attempt guard; replay is distinct from another live lease.

Six focused input-integrity, causal-binding, redaction and cache-identity tests
passed before execution. The final audit independently checked actual persisted
records and artifacts. Neither result establishes biological validity.
claim_reuse.author_response:
# Author response to the independent fin Claim-reuse review

October 31, 2026. This is a post-review clarification. It changes no frozen
protocol, Action/Evidence record, simulation output, producer receipt or review.
The producer's original readback remains a historical submission snapshot.

I read the review at commit
`c5d4163b35aa1a65dd8700b4242f1cbc195a669c`, including its findings and
`verify-output.json`. The reviewer reports separate closed-form/FEM calculations
and author-code replays supporting the two conditional numerical verdicts.
Reading those artifacts is not another independent rerun by the author.

The reviewer recorded both Evidence records as **disputed**: scoped computation
checks passed, while empirical relevance and independent replication remained
insufficient. That decision is preserved. Mathematical agreement between two
agent processes does not provide independent biological replication, measured
fin stiffness, fluid–structure validation or organism feasibility. The Actions
remain submitted in the review handoff; no author acceptance is requested here.

| Finding | Author clarification and remaining gap |
| --- | --- |
| Copied source-only limitation | Agreed. The statement that Frontier had not executed the calculation belongs to the **historical source Claim**, not these newly executed candidate Evidence records. The saved producer receipts and outputs document the actual bounded computations. The copied text is overly conservative and misleading in this new context. It is not silently rewritten; future Evidence construction should label inherited limitations by their source and add result-specific limits separately. |
| “Mesh convergence” | Agreed. For this uniform-load/constant-EI Hermite beam case, nodal results are exact up to numerical round-off. Agreement across 16/32/64 elements supports implementation/analytic consistency here; it establishes no convergence rate. Growing round-off with refinement is retained. The off-node profile check is also a numerical comparison for this case, not a general convergence theorem. |
| Claim-mutation refusals | Agreed. The altered Record fixtures were rejected at digest validation. This demonstrates integrity refusal, not independent execution of every downstream scope check. The L³ wrong-law control is a distinct solver/model mutation and remains separately recorded. A future isolated unit test could exercise the context-consistency condition with valid, deliberately constructed fixture records and matching test pins; that would be new evidence, not a retroactive claim about these runs. |
| Candidate margins in Action payloads | Agreed. The exact 9/10 and 11/10 choices were frozen in the pre-run protocol and retained in effective inputs; the revised Action cache identity commits to their protocol bytes. They were not separate human-readable numeric Action payload fields. Future proposals should expose these values directly as well as retaining the digest. No original Action is revised after execution. |

The narrow supported result remains: two distinct bounded computations consumed
the same exact Claim version before deriving EI and executing the installed beam
solver. For the declared surrogate, the 9/10 candidate exceeded the tip/span
limit and the 11/10 candidate remained inside the declared limits. This is actual
versioned reuse and a contribution/review workflow with a retained disagreement;
it is not evidence of collective benefit, agent superiority or a calibrated fin.

No further simulation, live credentialed write, acceptance-criterion change or
review-state mutation was performed for this response. The original 56-file
producer artifact manifest continues to describe its original snapshot; this
addendum is separate from that manifest and from the reviewer's artifacts.

The developmental-fin versus regeneration gap, scoped to the fish-fin trait bridge: PMC10211259 tests both developmental and regeneration enhancers in larval tissues, but no source read shows that any enhancer drives expression in the developing paired fin, or ties any enhancer to fin shape or stiffness.
Replicate independence of the multiome data is unconfirmed (metadata audit 1b77f81).

limbless.title: Limbless mouse
limbless.status: design space, mapped and partly simulated
limbless.goal: A judge asked whether we could make a limbless mouse. Rather than answer with one gene, map the whole design space: every route we can source, at every scale, with what each one would actually produce.
limbless.summary: There is no single answer. Published mouse genetics already contains alleles that remove limbs entirely, alleles that truncate them, and alleles that take one limb pair and leave the other. They sit at different scales and they are not interchangeable. This page lays the routes out side by side, runs the models we can run on three of them, and says plainly where the chain between scales is uncalibrated.

answer.headline: Yes, several ways — and they do not give you the same animal.
paragraphs: The honest answer to “could you make a limbless mouse?” is that the mouse literature already contains more than one way, and the first question back is which phenotype is wanted. Complete absence of all four limbs (amelia) is the Fgf10-null phenotype, and in humans the WNT3 Q83X tetra-amelia phenotype: the apical ectodermal ridge never forms, so there is no limb at all. Truncation is a different outcome reached by a different lesion: the limb bud starts, the SHH–GREM1–FGF loop fails to sustain it, and a stunted proximal element is left behind.

The sharpest precedent for getting there by editing regulation rather than by deleting a gene is Kvon et al. 2016. Replacing the mouse ZRS — the limb enhancer of Shh, about a megabase away inside an intron of Lmbr1 — with the king cobra ortholog abolished limb-bud Shh expression and truncated both limb pairs, while the human and coelacanth orthologs in the same assay gave normal limbs. And the 17 base pairs are not an association: Kvon et al. put that stretch, carrying an ETS site, back into the python ZRS, knocked that engineered allele into mice, and got normal limbs. Four ortholog knock-ins and one resurrected allele is the whole causal dataset, which is small — but it is a causal one. That is the resolution at which this is a design problem rather than a knockout.

If the goal is a viable adult animal rather than an embryonic phenotype, the realistic route is one limb pair, not four: a conditional Tbx5 allele for the forelimb, Tbx4 or Pitx1 for the hindlimb, switched after the body plan is laid down. Tetra-amelia alleles are generally severe and often lethal for reasons that have nothing to do with limbs.
And if the point is the mechanism rather than the mouse, the first thing a reviewer will ask for in 2026 is a limb-bud explant or organoid, not an animal. That route is on this page too.
answer.precision_note: Truncation is not amelia, and a page that blurs them is answering a question nobody asked. Every route below states which of the two — or which of micromelia, digit loss, or one-pair loss — it predicts.

scales.label: Molecular / sequence
scales.blurb: Change non-coding DNA and leave every protein intact. This is the layer where a limb can be removed without touching anything else the gene does, and it is the layer evolution used in snakes and sticklebacks. It is also the only layer a genome language model emits a score for.

scales.label: Gene / coding
scales.blurb: Delete or break the protein. The phenotypes here are the strongest and best documented, and most of them kill the animal for a reason that has nothing to do with limbs - lung, kidney, allantois, heart. The gene scale tells you what a node does; it rarely gives you an animal.

scales.label: Cell / signalling centre
scales.blurb: Remove or silence the AER or the ZPA as structures, rather than the genes that specify them. This is where the subject started, with a scalpel, and it is where the timing question is posed most directly: cut the ridge off later and you get more limb.

scales.label: Tissue / maintenance loop
scales.blurb: The circuit that decides how long the bud keeps growing: a SHH-GREM1-FGF loop that is self-promoting AND self-terminating, because rising FGF activity represses Grem1. It sets limb SIZE and when outgrowth stops. Nobody has shown that triggering it early removes a limb, and the page says so.

scales.label: Pattern formation
scales.blurb: The reaction-diffusion system that decides how many digits the autopod carries and how they are spaced: a BMP-SOX9-WNT Turing network whose wavelength distal Hox dose sets. This explains autopod FORM. Both published knobs move it toward MORE digits, not fewer, so nothing here has been shown to explain limb absence.

scales.label: Developmental timing
scales.blurb: Apply the lesion when you choose rather than at fertilisation. This is the scale that converts lethal mutants into viable animals and binary genotypes into ordered series, and it is where our recommendation sits. The same Tbx4 deletion gives blocked outgrowth, proximal hypoplasia, or nothing at all, depending only on the hour.

scales.label: Organism / evolutionary comparative
scales.blurb: Four independent natural limb losses - snakes, limb-reduced skinks, cetaceans, stickleback pelvis - solved by at least three different mechanisms at three different layers. They are the ground truth this subject has and ours does not, and they are the reason to present a design space instead of an answer.

scales.label: Non-animal / in vitro
scales.blurb: Budoids, human iPSC limb-bud mesenchyme, limb-bud explants, recombinant limbs and trunk-like structures. The route a modern reviewer asks about first, the route with the best welfare case, and the route whose honest limit is that no dish currently makes a limb.

chain.title: The chain across scales, and where it is not calibrated
chain.intro: The three models on this page are not independent demonstrations. They are meant to be read as one chain, and the chain has two junctions we refuse to call calibrated.

links.note: The sequence analysis measures divergence and motif content. It does not predict enhancer activity. Mapping an allele onto a fraction of wild-type Shh output is a scenario parameter, not a calibrated transfer.
This junction is inside the SHH–GREM1–FGF model, so it is at least explicit: the model says how a reduction in Shh production shortens the window in which FGF stays above threshold.
A shorter outgrowth window means a smaller paddle, but the model has no geometry. Converting one to the other needs a growth law we have not fitted.

This junction is inside the Turing model, which gives a critical domain size of about 0.94 ± 0.10 of the pattern's own wavelength — and finds that every route to zero elements in it is the same geometric condition, the Turing-permissive region having to be at least about one wavelength across.

chain.verdict: Two of the four junctions are within a single model and are explicit. Two cross between models and have no calibration behind them, so the end-to-end statement — “this allele gives that many digits” — is refused. The chain is a map of what would have to be measured, not a prediction.

not_claimed: No mouse was made, no embryo was used, and no wet-lab experiment was run for this page.
The three computational studies are simulations and a sequence analysis. None is an observation, and none is calibrated to a measured mouse limb bud.
No route on this page is a protocol. Each names published evidence and what would have to be done; none has been attempted here.
The sequence analysis is correlational over a handful of orthologs. It is not a predictor of enhancer activity and must not be used as one.
A threshold in a model is not a threshold in an embryo.

closing.title: Why this is on a design platform and not in a review article
closing.text: The useful thing here is not the list — a specialist could write the list. It is that every row carries its evidence level, every junction between scales carries a refusal or a label, and the three models can be re-run from the repository. The question “can you make a limbless mouse?” has a dozen answers whose differences only show up when you are forced to say which phenotype, at which scale, with what evidence, and at what cost. That is what this workspace is for.

routes.title: Replace the mouse ZRS with a snake ortholog (king cobra or Burmese python)
routes.mechanism: The ZRS is a limb-specific enhancer of Shh sitting ~1 Mb from the Shh promoter inside Lmbr1 intron 5, and it is the sole driver of Shh expression in the posterior limb bud mesenchyme. Snake ZRS orthologs have accumulated substitutions that destroy the transcription-factor binding sites the enhancer needs, so an otherwise wild-type mouse carrying a snake ZRS makes no limb-bud Shh. Every protein in the genome is left intact; only 1.3 kb of non-coding DNA changes.
routes.intervention: CRISPR/Cas9 homology-directed replacement of the functionally critical 1.3 kb ZRS core with the same-length orthologous sequence from king cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) or Burmese python (Python bivittatus). Kvon et al. did exactly this in FVB mice with a matched-littermate design.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Severe TRUNCATION of both fore- and hindlimbs, not amelia. The cobra knock-in gives complete loss of limb-bud Shh and a phenotype indistinguishable from deleting the enhancer outright; the proximal skeleton is present. The python knock-in is slightly milder: most elements distal to the stylopod:zeugopod junction are severely affected, but 2-3 rudimentary digits form in the forelimb and a slightly enlarged ossification resembling a rudimentary zeugopod appears, attributed to very weak residual Shh transcript detectable only after prolonged in-situ development.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11, 'Progressive Loss of Function in a Limb Enhancer during Snake Evolution'
evidence.finding: Replacing the mouse ZRS with the cobra ortholog 'resulted in a complete loss of [Shh] expression and a truncated limb phenotype, affecting both the fore- and hindlimbs, that is indistinguishable from the phenotype caused by deletion of the mouse enhancer'. The python ortholog gave 'a similar but a slightly milder phenotype ... 2-3 rudimentary digits in the forelimb'. Human and coelacanth orthologs rescued fully developed limbs.

routes.reversibility: Not reversible in the animal: this is a germline sequence change fixed at the zygote. It IS reversible at the design stage - reintroducing 17 bp restores normal limbs (see mol-zrs-e1-ets-site), which makes the allele series itself a dose knob rather than a switch.
routes.lethality_risk: Low. ZRS-null mice are alive and of comparable body size at two weeks of age; Kvon et al. photographed them. Mouse ZRS reporter assays show no reproducible activity outside the limb and ZRS deletion studies report no phenotypes beyond limb defects, so there is no known non-limb organ requirement.
routes.specificity: Limb only, both pairs, posterior-distal. It removes the autopod and zeugopod and spares the stylopod and girdle. It does not touch lung, kidney, allantois, neural tube or craniofacial structures.
routes.difficulty: low-to-medium. The exact sgRNA, donor design, homology arms and genotyping primers are published; the line already exists in at least one lab. Cost is a standard CRISPR knock-in campaign plus a mouse colony.
routes.what_we_would_run:
Score the published ortholog series with a genome language model (we have an Evo 2 7B pipeline that has produced one real paired result on zebrafish regulatory windows) and ask whether the model's ranking reproduces the measured ranking: human ~ coelacanth (normal) > python (weak residual) > cobra (none). Pre-register the prediction. Controls: dinucleotide shuffles and GC-matched random windows, as in the run we already did.

STUDY: The study `zrs-conservation` IS this route's assay: it is the ZRS ortholog panel, and the measured knock-in ranking (human ~ coelacanth normal > python weak residual > cobra none) is the answer key any score would be checked against.
open_questions: Does a sequence model separate cobra from coelacanth, given that coelacanth shares LESS sequence identity with human ZRS (57%) than python does (59%) yet behaves like wild type? This is the single sharpest test in the dataset and it is an explicit identity-versus-function dissociation.
Boa ZRS retained ZPA reporter activity but was never taken to knock-in, so the 'ordered series' is four knock-in phenotypes plus reporter data, not a uniform assay.

routes.title: Delete the ZRS outright
routes.mechanism: Removing the enhancer removes the only known driver of limb-bud Shh. Shh protein is still made everywhere else it is normally made (notochord, floor plate, gut), so the animal has no midline, neural-tube or axial defect. This is the cleanest available dissociation between 'Shh the gene' and 'Shh in the limb'.
routes.intervention: CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of the 1,324 bp ZRS (mm10 chr5:29,314,497-29,315,820), or the earlier targeted deletion of the conserved intronic module. Both alleles exist.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Truncation of both limbs with a surviving proximal skeleton. At E18.5 the forelimb humerus, radius and ulna appear fused and no recognisable autopod is present; the hindlimb zeugopod is severely reduced and the autopod is represented by a single rudimentary digit. Animals survive to at least two weeks with body size comparable to wild type.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11
evidence.finding: Figure S3E-F: 'Gross phenotypes of two week old ZRS(+/+) (top) and ZRS(-/-) (bottom) mice. The body sizes are comparable, but ZRS(-/-) mice have truncated limbs.' Skeletal detail as described above.

evidence.cite: Sagai T et al. 2005, Development 132:797-803, 'Elimination of a long-range cis-regulatory module causes complete loss of limb-specific Shh expression and truncation of the mouse limb'
evidence.finding: Targeted deletion of the conserved intronic sequence gives 'a complete loss of Shh expression in the limb bud and degeneration of skeletal elements distal to the stylopod/zygopod junction'.

routes.reversibility: None in the animal. Germline, constitutive.
routes.lethality_risk: Low; this is the only route in the whole design space with a published photograph of a limb-reduced mouse alive at two weeks and of normal body size.
routes.specificity: Limb only, both pairs. Spares girdle and stylopod.
routes.difficulty: low. Two independent alleles published, one of them CRISPR-made specifically to exclude neo-cassette and background effects.
routes.what_we_would_run:
Nothing new computationally - this is the reference phenotype everything else is scored against, and it is the anchor for the honest claim that 'limbless mouse' in the ZRS literature means limb-REDUCED and viable, not amelia.

STUDY: `zrs-conservation` bears on this route as its anchor: the ZRS-null is the wild-type-to-null endpoint the ortholog series is read against, and it is the reference phenotype for the whole molecular scale.
open_questions: Welfare: a viable animal with truncated limbs is the ethically harder case precisely because it lives. See the welfare section.
No published long-term (adult, >2 week) husbandry or behavioural data was found in our search.

routes.title: Edit the single E1 ETS binding site - a 17 bp switch
routes.mechanism: A 17 bp deletion overlapping the E1 ETS1 recognition motif is the only sequence present in all examined limbed vertebrates and fish and absent from all examined snakes. Reintroducing those 17 bp into an otherwise-python ZRS restores full enhancer activity in the posterior limb-bud mesenchyme and rescues normal limb development in the mouse. Conversely the site is the smallest known handle on the whole system.
routes.intervention: CRISPR knock-in of a 1,341 bp synthetic 'resurrected python' allele (python ZRS plus the 17 bp lizard sequence) in place of the mouse ZRS; or the reciprocal, removing the 17 bp from an otherwise wild-type mouse ZRS.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Reintroduction direction: NORMAL limbs. Removal direction: Kvon et al. state that loss of the E1 motif in the mouse ZRS alone is NOT sufficient to alter limb-bud expression, and boa ZRS is active despite lacking both E0 and E1, so deleting E1 in mouse is predicted to give normal or near-normal limbs. Do not state that removing 17 bp from a mouse removes its limbs; the literature says the opposite.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11
evidence.finding: 'reintroduction of 17 bp of sequence alone was sufficient to reinstate full enhancer activity' and knock-in mice with the modified python allele 'had normal limbs'. Separately: 'the loss of E1 motif in mouse ZRS is not sufficient to alter limb bud expression' and boa ZRS is active despite lacking E0 and E1, so 'loss of these motifs alone cannot explain ZRS deactivation in snake lineage'.

routes.reversibility: This is the one asymmetric, directional result in the design space: the 17 bp is sufficient to RESTORE function on a degraded background but not sufficient to DESTROY function on a healthy one. Context-dependence of this kind is exactly what a per-nucleotide additive sequence model will get wrong.
routes.lethality_risk: None beyond the background allele.
routes.specificity: Limb only.
routes.difficulty: low. Published allele, published sequence.
routes.what_we_would_run:
Ask a genome language model for the effect of the 17 bp indel in BOTH directions and on BOTH backgrounds (mouse ZRS minus 17 bp; python ZRS plus 17 bp). A model that reports a symmetric effect has failed a test with a known answer. This is a cheap, pre-registerable, falsifiable experiment, and the published asymmetry means we know the right answer before scoring.

STUDY: `zrs-conservation` bears on this route directly, and this is the sharpest test in it: the 17 bp E1 indel has a published ASYMMETRIC effect, so a model scored on that panel has a known-in-advance right answer to fail.
open_questions: Kvon et al. explicitly say ETS-site loss alone cannot explain snake ZRS deactivation and point at homeodomain motifs with a similar snake-specific substitution increase. So E1 is necessary-in-context, not the mechanism.

routes.title: Design a graded ZRS hypomorphic allelic series from the in-vivo variant panel
routes.mechanism: Nearly a thousand human ZRS variants have been assayed in vivo in a high-throughput mouse reporter, and selected variants were confirmed in knock-in mice. That panel is a measured sequence-to-activity map over the exact element that sets limb-bud Shh. In principle one can pick combinations that place enhancer activity at a chosen point between wild type and null and so dial the degree of limb reduction.
routes.intervention: Select variant combinations from the published panel, knock them in, and read out skeletal phenotype at E18.5.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Unknown and the honest answer is that the published panel points the WRONG WAY for this purpose. Kvon et al. 2020 assayed an enhancer 'repeatedly linked to polydactyly' and the knock-in confirmations were of variants that CAUSE polydactyly - a gain of ectopic anterior activity, i.e. extra digits, not fewer. A graded loss-of-function series would have to be designed and tested; it does not exist in that dataset.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2020, Cell 180:1262-1271.e15, 'Comprehensive In Vivo Interrogation Reveals Phenotypic Impact of Human Enhancer Variants'
evidence.finding: '71% of all rare non-coding variants previously proposed as causal lead to reporter gene expression in a pattern consistent with their pathogenic role. Variants observed to alter enhancer activity were further confirmed to cause polydactyly in knockin mice.' Combinatorial and single-nucleotide mutagenesis covered all positions of the enhancer.

evidence.cite: Gurnett CA et al. 2007, Am J Med Genet A 143A:27-32, 'Two novel point mutations in the long-range SHH enhancer in three families with triphalangeal thumb and preaxial polydactyly'
evidence.finding: Point mutations within the ZRS (bp 621, bp 739 of a 774 bp conserved core in LMBR1 intron 5) segregate with triphalangeal thumb and preaxial polydactyly; both alter putative Cdx binding sites. A 5'-end mutation was associated with a milder phenotype and 82% penetrance.

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.lethality_risk: Low, by analogy with the deletion.
routes.specificity: Limb only.
routes.difficulty: high, because the loss-of-function side of the map is not the side that was measured. Building it means a new in-vivo panel.
routes.what_we_would_run:
Score the Kvon 2020 panel and report rank correlation against the published in-vivo calls - but label it for what it is: a benchmark on the POLYDACTYLY (gain) direction, used as a proxy for whether the model has any grip on this element at all. Reporting it as a limb-loss benchmark would be a category error.

STUDY: `zrs-conservation` bears on this route, but only on its gain-of-function half - the panel it would be scored against was assayed for polydactyly, not limb reduction, and that has to be stated wherever the number is reported.
open_questions: Is a model that ranks gain-of-function ZRS variants well also good at loss-of-function ZRS variants? Nothing in the literature we read answers this, and assuming transfer is exactly the kind of assumption that has failed before.

routes.title: Break the CTCF-mediated contact between the ZRS and the SHH promoter
routes.mechanism: The ZRS acts across ~1 Mb, and that action depends on physical contact. Three CTCF sites inside a 12 kb interval of LMBR1 mediate the ZRS-to-SHH-promoter interaction. Homozygous deletion of that interval in humans causes acheiropodia, congenital limb truncation, and the interval does not itself function as an enhancer - the lesion is architectural, not transcriptional.
routes.intervention: Delete or mutate the CTCF sites that anchor the ZRS-promoter loop, leaving the enhancer sequence intact.
routes.predicted_phenotype: In humans: acheiropodia - congenital truncation of hands and feet. In mouse: NO APPARENT ABNORMALITY. This route is the design space's clearest documented failure of species transfer.

evidence.cite: Ushiki A et al. 2021, Nat Commun 12:2282, 'Deletion of CTCF sites in the SHH locus alters enhancer-promoter interactions and leads to acheiropodia'
evidence.finding: Fine-mapped the acheiropodia region to 12 kb; it does not function as an enhancer. Three CTCF sites mediate the ZRS-SHH promoter interaction, substituted by centromeric sites in disease. 'Mouse knockouts of the orthologous 12 kb sequence have no apparent abnormalities, showcasing the challenges in modelling CTCF alterations in animal models due to inherent motif differences between species.'

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable in mouse (no phenotype). In humans acheiropodia is compatible with life.
routes.specificity: Would be limb-restricted if it worked, because the contact being broken is the limb enhancer's.
routes.difficulty: high, and currently unsolved: nobody has engineered a mouse allele that reproduces the human architectural lesion. It would require re-deriving the CTCF motif arrangement for the mouse locus rather than copying the human deletion.
routes.what_we_would_run: Encode this as an explicit REFUSAL in our cross-scale coupling layer: a human-to-mouse transfer of a CTCF-motif-dependent claim is not composable, and the layer should say so with the Ushiki result as the stated reason rather than emitting a score. This is a one-record change and it is the kind of thing the layer exists for. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Which mouse CTCF sites would have to be removed to phenocopy acheiropodia? Nobody has published an answer.
Would a sequence model trained on human data flag the mouse orthologous deletion as benign? If it does, that is the correct answer and worth demonstrating.

routes.title: Move a TAD boundary so the limb enhancer cluster drives the wrong gene
routes.mechanism: Limb enhancers are confined to a topologically associating domain by CTCF-associated boundaries. Deletions, inversions and duplications that disrupt those boundaries let a cluster of limb enhancers contact a promoter it should never reach, producing ectopic limb expression of the wrong gene. The rewiring occurs only when the variant disrupts a CTCF-associated boundary - the structural change, not the sequence content, is the lesion.
routes.intervention: CRISPR engineering of deletions, inversions or duplications at a TAD boundary, modelled on the human WNT6/IHH/EPHA4/PAX3 rearrangements, which were reproduced as mouse alleles.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Limb MALFORMATION of a type set by which gene is misexpressed (the published human conditions at this locus are brachydactyly, polydactyly and syndactyly) - not limb loss. This route is in the design space because it is the general architectural mechanism and because it is mouse-validated, not because it has been shown to remove a limb.

evidence.cite: Lupianez DG et al. 2015, Cell 161:1012-1025, 'Disruptions of topological chromatin domains cause pathogenic rewiring of gene-enhancer interactions'
evidence.finding: Distinct human limb malformations are caused by deletions, inversions or duplications altering the TAD-spanning WNT6/IHH/EPHA4/PAX3 locus; CRISPR mice with corresponding rearrangements showed ectopic promoter-noncoding contacts and ectopic limb expression. 'This rewiring occurred only if the variant disrupted a CTCF-associated boundary domain.'

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.lethality_risk: Locus-dependent; the published alleles are viable.
routes.specificity: Depends entirely on which domain is broken. A boundary move is a blunt instrument: it changes everything in the domain, not one enhancer-promoter pair.
routes.difficulty: high. Large structural variants are harder to make and harder to genotype than a 1.3 kb replacement, and the outcome is not predictable from sequence alone.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing yet. A sequence model that scores 1 kb windows has no representation of a megabase-scale boundary, so this route is a good argument for why 'score the enhancer' is not the same as 'predict the phenotype', and it belongs on the page as that argument. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Can any current sequence model predict the direction of a boundary-disruption phenotype? We found no evidence that one can, and our search did not cover the chromatin-model literature.

routes.title: Delete the Pitx1 hindlimb enhancer - nature's own cis-regulatory limb removal
routes.mechanism: In threespine stickleback, pelvic (hindlimb-homologue) loss has evolved repeatedly through deletion of a tissue-specific enhancer of Pitx1. Pitx1 null alleles are lethal in laboratory animals; the enhancer deletion is not, and it carries molecular signatures of positive selection. This is the proof of principle that evolution solves 'remove an appendage without killing the animal' by cis-regulation, not by knockout.
routes.intervention: Identify and delete the mouse orthologous hindlimb-specific Pitx1 enhancer. The stickleback element is characterised; the mouse equivalent would have to be mapped, which is work, not a copy.
routes.predicted_phenotype: In stickleback: pelvic reduction/loss, viable, naturally selected. In mouse: UNKNOWN and not to be asserted. The best-supported expectation is a hindlimb-restricted phenotype milder than the Pitx1 null (which gives hindlimb hypoplasia, not absence), but we found no published mouse Pitx1 limb-enhancer deletion.

evidence.cite: Chan YF et al. 2010, Science 327:302-5, 'Adaptive evolution of pelvic reduction in sticklebacks by recurrent deletion of a Pitx1 enhancer'
evidence.finding: Pelvic loss in different natural stickleback populations occurred through regulatory mutations deleting a tissue-specific Pitx1 enhancer. 'Although Pitx1 null mutations are lethal in laboratory animals, Pitx1 regulatory mutations show molecular signatures of positive selection in pelvic-reduced populations.' Deletion is recurrent, possibly from structural features of the locus.

evidence.cite: Lanctot C et al. 1999, Development 126:1805-10, 'Hindlimb patterning and mandible development require the Ptx1 gene'
evidence.finding: Mouse Pitx1 (Ptx1) null: hindlimb development severely impaired but not abolished - ilium and knee cartilage absent, long bones underdeveloped, Tbx4 expression decreased; also loss of proximal mandibular bones. Limb-bud molecular identity is retained.

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.specificity: Hindlimb only, if the mouse element behaves like the stickleback one. Note the mouse Pitx1 null ALSO loses proximal mandibular bone, so the gene is not hindlimb-exclusive even if the enhancer is.
routes.lethality_risk: Low for an enhancer deletion by the stickleback precedent; high for the null in laboratory animals per Chan et al.
routes.difficulty: high, because the mouse enhancer has to be found first and the Ushiki result (above) is a standing warning that a cis-element's behaviour does not transfer between species.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the single best test case for a sequence model doing something useful rather than reproducing a known answer: use the model to nominate candidate hindlimb-specific Pitx1 enhancers in mouse, then check the nominations against published limb-bud ATAC/ChIP data. That is a retrieval task with an external answer key, not a self-graded one. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Is there a single mouse Pitx1 hindlimb enhancer, or distributed redundancy? Enhancer redundancy is the standard reason a cis-deletion gives no phenotype, and we did not search the Pitx1 regulatory-landscape literature.

routes.title: Fgf10 germline null - the canonical tetra-amelia mouse
routes.mechanism: FGF10 is the mesenchymal signal that induces and sustains the apical ectodermal ridge (AER); it acts epistatically upstream of Fgf8, the earliest AER marker. Without it the AER never forms, the ZPA never forms, and the limb bud makes no outgrowth. The same ligand drives branching morphogenesis in lung, so the mouse has no lungs either.
routes.intervention: Germline Fgf10 knockout (two independent lines published, 1998 and 1999).
routes.predicted_phenotype: AMELIA. Fetuses develop to birth with complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs. The clavicle is unaffected (it is a dermal bone of different origin). Perinatal lethal from complete absence of lungs: the trachea forms, main-stem bronchial formation and all subsequent branching do not.

evidence.cite: Min H et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:3156-61, 'Fgf-10 is required for both limb and lung development...'
evidence.finding: 'Limb bud initiation was abolished in Fgf-10(-/-) mice. Strikingly, Fgf-10(-/-) fetuses continued to develop until birth, despite the complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs. Fgf-10 is necessary for apical ectodermal ridge (AER) formation and acts epistatically upstream of Fgf-8.' Perinatal lethality with complete absence of lungs.

evidence.cite: Sekine K et al. 1999, Nat Genet 21:138-41, 'Fgf10 is essential for limb and lung formation'
evidence.finding: 'complete truncation of the fore- and hindlimbs. In Fgf10-/- embryos, limb bud formation was initiated but outgrowth of the limb buds did not occur ... the apical ectodermal ridge (AER) and the zone of polarizing activity (ZPA) did not form'; clavicle formation unaffected; died at birth from lack of lung development.

routes.reversibility: None. Germline, constitutive, and the animal cannot be rescued because the lung defect is independent of the limb defect.
routes.lethality_risk: HIGH and certain: perinatal lethal from lung agenesis. No Fgf10-null mouse has ever drawn a breath, so there is no viable limbless adult by this route.
routes.specificity: Poor. FGF10 is the major ligand for FGFR2b across many organs: Fgf10-null mice also lack thyroid, pituitary and salivary glands, with minor defects in teeth, kidney, hair follicles and digestive organs.
routes.difficulty: low to make, impossible to make viable as a constitutive allele. The conditional version is the route worth proposing (see timing-prx1-creer-fgf10).
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing computational adds value here; this is the ground-truth amelia phenotype the whole page is calibrated against. If the judge's mice were tetra-amelic AND died at birth, this is the likely mechanism class. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: The two founding papers DISAGREE about whether the limb bud initiates: Min et al. say initiation was abolished; Sekine et al. say bud formation initiated but outgrowth did not occur. We preserve that disagreement rather than reconciling it, and it matters because it decides whether the lesion is in induction or in maintenance.

routes.title: Fgfr2-IIIb (FGFR2b) isoform null - the receptor side of the same axis
routes.mechanism: Fgfr2 is alternatively spliced into IIIb and IIIc isoforms with different ligand specificities and mutually exclusive tissue distributions. FGFR2b is the epithelial receptor that reads mesenchymal FGF10. Removing only IIIb leaves IIIc intact and so removes one arm of the mesenchymal-epithelial dialogue rather than the whole receptor.
routes.intervention: Cre-mediated excision of the IIIb exon, retaining IIIc expression.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Severe limb defects with a distinctive time course: 'development of these structures appears to initiate, but then fails with the tissues undergoing extensive apoptosis'. Viable until birth. Also severe lung and anterior pituitary defects, plus salivary gland, inner ear, tooth, skin and minor skull abnormalities.

evidence.cite: De Moerlooze L et al. 2000, Development 127:483-92, 'An important role for the IIIb isoform of fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) in mesenchymal-epithelial signalling during mouse organogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'Fibroblast growth factor receptor 2(IIIb) null mice are viable until birth, but have severe defects of the limbs, lung and anterior pituitary gland. The development of these structures appears to initiate, but then fails with the tissues undergoing extensive apoptosis.'

evidence.cite: Ohuchi H et al. 2000, Biochem Biophys Res Commun 277:643-9, 'FGF10 acts as a major ligand for FGF receptor 2 IIIb in mouse multi-organ development'
evidence.finding: Fgf10-null phenotypes closely parallel FGFR2b-deficient phenotypes across many organs (absent thyroid, pituitary, salivary glands), supporting FGF10 as the major FGFR2b ligand in organogenesis.

routes.reversibility: None as a germline allele.
routes.lethality_risk: High - viable until birth only, with lung and pituitary agenesis.
routes.specificity: Poor; multi-organ, by construction (the whole point of the receptor is that it serves many epithelia).
routes.difficulty: low to make; same viability dead end as Fgf10.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing new. This route earns its place by being the mechanistic mirror of Fgf10 and by showing that 'initiates then apoptoses' is a THIRD phenotypic class distinct from both amelia and truncation - a distinction the existing dossier does not draw. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Is the limb defect in Fgfr2-IIIb nulls the same as the Fgf10 null, or milder because other FGFR2b ligands partially compensate? The abstracts do not settle it and we did not read the bodies.

routes.title: Ectodermal WNT3 / beta-catenin - the human tetra-amelia gene
routes.mechanism: Wnt3 is expressed ubiquitously in limb ectoderm and signals through beta-catenin to establish the AER; beta-catenin is also required continuously to MAINTAIN the ridge once induced. Wnt/beta-catenin sits upstream of BMP signalling in AER establishment and interacts with BMPR1A in dorsoventral patterning. In humans a homozygous nonsense allele of WNT3 causes complete absence of all four limbs.
routes.intervention: Mouse: Wnt3 loss, or conditional removal of beta-catenin from ventral limb ectoderm (before induction to prevent the AER, after induction to make an existing AER disappear). Human: the natural WNT3 Q83X allele.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Human WNT3 Q83X homozygotes: TETRA-AMELIA - complete absence of all four limbs, with craniofacial and urogenital defects. Mouse: AER fails to be established; removing beta-catenin after induction makes an existing AER disappear, giving a later and milder truncation. Note Wnt3-null mice are reported early-lethal, which is why the human allele is the informative one.

evidence.cite: Niemann S et al. 2004, Am J Hum Genet 74:558-63, 'Homozygous WNT3 mutation causes tetra-amelia in a large consanguineous family'
evidence.finding: Homozygous nonsense mutation Q83X in WNT3 in four affected fetuses with autosomal recessive tetra-amelia plus craniofacial and urogenital defects. 'Our findings contrast with the observation of early lethality in mice homozygous for null alleles of Wnt3.' First WNT-gene mutation associated with a Mendelian disorder.

evidence.cite: Barrow JR et al. 2003, Genes Dev 17:394-409, 'Ectodermal Wnt3/beta-catenin signaling is required for the establishment and maintenance of the apical ectodermal ridge'
evidence.finding: Conditional removal of beta-catenin in ventral ectodermal cells is sufficient to elicit the mutant limb phenotype; removing beta-catenin AFTER ridge induction results in the disappearance of the AER. Wnt/beta-catenin lies upstream of BMP in AER establishment.

evidence.cite: Soshnikova N et al. 2003, Genes Dev 17:1963-8, 'Genetic interaction between Wnt/beta-catenin and BMP receptor signaling during formation of the AER and the dorsal-ventral axis in the limb'
evidence.finding: beta-catenin is a key regulator of AER formation and of limb dorsoventral axis; it acts downstream of BMPR1A in AER induction but upstream or parallel in dorsoventral patterning.

routes.reversibility: The beta-catenin conditional is the reversible-in-principle version and the only published demonstration that an ALREADY FORMED AER can be made to disappear - which is the cell-biological basis for every timing route on this page.
routes.lethality_risk: High for germline Wnt3 (early embryonic lethal in mouse). The ectoderm-restricted beta-catenin conditional avoids that.
routes.specificity: beta-catenin is the least specific molecule in this entire design space - it is the canonical WNT effector in essentially every tissue. Restriction comes entirely from the Cre driver, not from the gene.
routes.difficulty: medium. Floxed beta-catenin and limb-ectoderm Cre drivers are standard.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing new computationally. The value of this route on the page is that it names the human condition the judge is most likely to have in mind if their work is human genetics, and that it separates AER ESTABLISHMENT from AER MAINTENANCE as two different targets. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: The human-versus-mouse viability discordance for WNT3 is flagged by Niemann et al. themselves and is a second instance of the Ushiki lesson: the same gene, two species, different tolerability.

routes.title: RSPO2 / RNF43 / ZNRF3 - the master switch for limb specification
routes.mechanism: RSPO2 potentiates WNT signalling. An allelic series of recessive human RSPO2 mutations causes tetra-amelia syndrome with lung aplasia, with severity correlating with impaired binding to LGR4/5/6 and to the RNF43 and ZNRF3 transmembrane ligases. Unexpectedly, triple knockout of Lgr4/5/6 in mice does NOT reproduce the Rspo2 phenotype; instead RSPO2 acts as a direct antagonistic ligand of RNF43 and ZNRF3, and deleting rnf43 and znrf3 together in Xenopus triggers outgrowth of SUPERNUMERARY limbs.
routes.intervention: Mouse: Rspo2 loss of function, or an allelic series modelled on the human mutations. The reciprocal (deleting Rnf43/Znrf3) is the limb-ADDITION direction and is the cleanest published demonstration that this node is a bidirectional switch.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Human RSPO2 loss of function: tetra-amelia syndrome - 'lung aplasia and a total absence of the four limbs'. The published allelic series means severity is graded, not binary. In mouse, the corresponding Rspo2 limb phenotype is not stated in the abstract we read; we would not assert it.

evidence.cite: Szenker-Ravi E et al. 2018, Nature 557:564-569, 'RSPO2 inhibition of RNF43 and ZNRF3 governs limb development independently of LGR4/5/6'
evidence.finding: 'an allelic series of recessive RSPO2 mutations in humans that cause tetra-amelia syndrome, which is characterized by lung aplasia and a total absence of the four limbs'; severity correlated with binding and WNT-potentiation defects. 'the concurrent deletion of rnf43 and znrf3 in Xenopus embryos was sufficient to trigger the outgrowth of supernumerary limbs. Our results establish that RSPO2 ... serves as a direct antagonistic ligand to RNF43 and ZNRF3, which together constitute a master switch that governs limb specification.'

routes.reversibility: Conceptually the most reversible node in the design space, because it is a ligand-receptor antagonism rather than a transcriptional commitment: the Xenopus result shows the switch can be driven in the gain direction too. Whether that is tractable in mouse is untested.
routes.lethality_risk: High in the full loss-of-function state - lung aplasia accompanies the human amelia, the same coupling as Fgf10. A graded allele from the human series is the way round it, which is what makes the allelic series valuable.
routes.specificity: Whole-organism WNT modulation; not limb-restricted.
routes.difficulty: medium-high. Point alleles from the human series are straightforward to knock in; interpreting them needs the lung phenotype controlled.
routes.what_we_would_run: If a sequence/protein model is going to be tested on 'does this variant abolish limb development', the RSPO2 allelic series is a better-posed coding benchmark than anything in the ZRS literature, because severity is graded, the biochemistry is measured per allele, and the phenotype is recorded per family. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: What is the mouse Rspo2 limb phenotype, and does it match the human? We did not retrieve it; stating it would be fabrication.
This gene is absent from the existing dossier and is arguably a stronger candidate than WNT3 for 'the gene for limblessness' in human genetics.

routes.title: Tbx5 - forelimb only, and the cleanest single-pair route
routes.mechanism: TBX5 is expressed exclusively in the prospective forelimb mesenchyme before any bud is visible. It directly activates Fgf10 through a conserved binding site, which is how it initiates the FGF/WNT loop. Critically, the limb FIELD is still patterned correctly in its absence: the territory is specified, the bud is simply never started. Tbx5 is also required later for continued outgrowth.
routes.intervention: Germline Tbx5 null, or Cre-conditional deletion in the forelimb field. Human TBX5 haploinsufficiency gives Holt-Oram syndrome (upper-limb and heart defects), which is a much milder phenotype and should not be quoted as limblessness.
routes.predicted_phenotype: FORELIMB BUDS DO NOT FORM. Hindlimbs are normal. Patterning of the lateral plate mesoderm into the limb field is intact; the FGF and Wnt regulatory loops are never established, including initiation of Fgf10 expression. Early forelimb-versus-hindlimb identity is not disturbed.

evidence.cite: Agarwal P et al. 2003, Development 130:623-33, 'Tbx5 is essential for forelimb bud initiation following patterning of the limb field in the mouse embryo'
evidence.finding: 'mouse embryos lacking Tbx5 do not form forelimb buds, although the patterning of the lateral plate mesoderm into the limb field is intact. Tbx5 is not essential for an early establishment of forelimb versus hindlimb identity. In the absence of Tbx5, the FGF and Wnt regulatory loops required for limb bud outgrowth are not established, including initiation of Fgf10 expression. Tbx5 directly activates the Fgf10 gene via a conserved binding site.'

evidence.cite: Rallis C et al. 2003, Development 130:2741-51, 'Tbx5 is required for forelimb bud formation and continued outgrowth'
evidence.finding: Conditional knockout in the developing forelimb shows Tbx5 is required at early limb bud stages for forelimb bud development; dominant-negative/dominant-active misexpression in chick wing shows a further requirement at later stages for continued outgrowth. Human TBX5 haploinsufficiency causes Holt-Oram syndrome.

routes.reversibility: A conditional allele plus an inducible Cre makes this the best-documented STAGE-SELECTABLE single-pair route, because Rallis et al. show there are two separable requirements (initiation and continued outgrowth).
routes.lethality_risk: Medium. TBX5 is a cardiac transcription factor and the germline null has heart defects; a limb-restricted conditional removes that problem. This is the whole argument for conditional over germline.
routes.specificity: Forelimb only - the single most specific route in the gene scale. Hindlimbs untouched.
routes.difficulty: low-medium. Floxed Tbx5 and limb Cre drivers are standard reagents.
routes.what_we_would_run: Our pattern simulators can model an initiation failure (no FGF10 source) versus a maintenance failure (source decays) and ask whether the two give distinguishable bud-size trajectories. That is a model-internal claim about our own simulator, not a claim about mice, and we would label it as such. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: A forelimb-only animal still has hindlimbs and so can locomote, thermoregulate and reach food - which is why this route, not tetra-amelia, is the one with a plausible welfare case. Whether a mouse without forelimbs can groom adequately is a question for a veterinary assessment, not for us.

routes.title: Tbx4 (with Pitx1) - hindlimb only, and a very narrow time window
routes.mechanism: Tbx4 is the hindlimb counterpart of Tbx5 and is required for hindlimb bud outgrowth; Pitx1 sits with it in the posterior lateral plate and determines hindlimb morphological identity. The conditional analysis is the interesting part: ablating Tbx4 before hindlimb-field expression blocks outgrowth, ablating it shortly after onset leaves outgrowth and Fgf10 expression unaffected but reduces limb core tissue, and ablating it later produces no defect at all.
routes.intervention: Germline Tbx4 null; or the conditional allele ablated at chosen stages; or Pitx1 null. Pitx1 misexpression in the forelimb transforms forelimb muscle, tendon and bone towards hindlimb morphology, so the gene is a morphology switch in both directions.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Tbx4 null: the hindlimb field IS induced and initial bud patterning appears normal, but buds fail to develop and do not maintain Fgf10; embryos die by E10.5 from failed chorioallantoic fusion, with stunted apoptotic allantoises and no vascular remodelling. Pitx1 null: hindlimb development severely impaired but NOT abolished - ilium and knee cartilage absent, long bones underdeveloped, Tbx4 reduced. Tbx4 loss does not alter hindlimb IDENTITY by morphology or molecular markers.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2003, Development 130:2681-93, 'Loss of Tbx4 blocks hindlimb development and affects vascularization and fusion of the allantois'
evidence.finding: Homozygous nulls 'fail to undergo chorioallantoic fusion and die by 10.5 days post coitus'. 'Induction of a hindlimb field occurs normally in Tbx4 mutants and initial patterning of the hindlimb bud appears normal. However, hindlimb buds from Tbx4 mutants fail to develop either in vivo or in vitro and do not maintain Fgf10 expression in the mesenchyme.'

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2007, Development 134:93-103, 'Tbx4 is not required for hindlimb identity or post-bud hindlimb outgrowth'
evidence.finding: Ablation before hindlimb-field expression confirms a requirement for bud outgrowth; ablation shortly after onset 'alters neither limb outgrowth nor expression of Fgf10' but gives reduced limb core tissue and proximal hypoplasia; later loss 'produces no limb defects, revealing a brief developmental requirement for Tbx4 function'. Loss of Tbx4 has no effect on hindlimb identity.

evidence.cite: Lanctot C et al. 1999, Development 126:1805-10
evidence.finding: Pitx1 null: hindlimb severely impaired not abolished; ilium and knee cartilage absent; also loss of proximal mandible-derived bones.
