evidence.cite: DeLaurier A, Schweitzer R & Logan M 2006, Dev Biol 299:22-34, 'Pitx1 determines the morphology of muscle, tendon, and bones of the hindlimb'
evidence.finding: Misexpression of Pitx1 in the forelimb transforms and translocates specific muscles, tendons and bones toward hindlimb-like morphology and upregulates Hoxc10 and Tbx4; misexpression of Tbx4 does not. 'Pitx1, but not Tbx4, determines the morphological identity of hindlimb tissues.'

routes.reversibility: The published conditional series is the point: there is a brief window in which Tbx4 matters and outside it the gene is dispensable. That is a real, measured timing knob, not a proposal.
routes.lethality_risk: The germline Tbx4 null is lethal at E10.5 for an allantoic reason entirely unrelated to limbs - a textbook case of a non-limb phenotype masquerading as a limb result. The conditional allele is what makes the route usable at all.
routes.specificity: Hindlimb only, if conditional. The germline allele also hits the allantois; Pitx1 also hits the mandible.
routes.difficulty: medium. Conditional allele and stage-specific Cre both published.
routes.what_we_would_run: Encode the Tbx4 timing result as a test case for our coupling layer: the SAME genetic lesion produces three different phenotypes depending only on when it is applied. Any claim of the form 'gene X -> phenotype Y' that carries no time index should be refused by the layer, and this is the cleanest published example to anchor that rule on. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Is there an equivalently narrow window for Tbx5 in the forelimb? Rallis et al. report two requirements but we did not find a stage-resolved series as fine as Naiche's.

routes.title: Meis1 + Meis2 in the lateral plate mesoderm - limb agenesis upstream of everything
routes.mechanism: MEIS factors act before limb induction. They co-bind genomic sites extensively with TBX factors and co-regulate Fgf10 enhancers, so removing both from the lateral plate mesoderm removes the input that lets Tbx5/Tbx4 start a bud at all. A partial allele also disrupts the antero-posterior prepattern that Shh activation depends on, which is a second, separable requirement.
routes.intervention: Conditional inactivation of Meis1 and Meis2 in the lateral plate mesoderm; or a three-deleted-allele hypomorph for the graded version.
routes.predicted_phenotype: LIMB AGENESIS (both pairs) on full inactivation in the LPM. Three-deleted-allele limbs show proximal-specific skeletal hypoplasia and agenesis of POSTERIOR skeletal elements, from failure to establish the AP prepattern needed for Shh activation. So the same gene pair gives agenesis or a graded posterior loss depending on dose.

evidence.cite: Delgado I et al. 2021, Nat Commun 12:3086, 'Control of mouse limb initiation and antero-posterior patterning by Meis transcription factors'
evidence.finding: 'Meis1/2 inactivation in the lateral plate mesoderm of mouse embryos leads to limb agenesis. Meis and Tbx factors converge in this function, extensively co-binding with Tbx to genomic sites and co-regulating enhancers of Fgf10 ... Limbs with three deleted Meis alleles show proximal-specific skeletal hypoplasia and agenesis of posterior skeletal elements.'

evidence.cite: Berenguer M & Duester G 2021, Biomolecules 11:80, 'Role of Retinoic Acid Signaling, FGF Signaling and Meis Genes in Control of Limb Development' (review)
evidence.finding: Review arguing that activation of FGF10 signalling is required for limb-bud emergence, with Tbx5/RA upstream in the forelimb field and Tbx4/Pitx1 upstream in the hindlimb field; and that limb Meis expression is activated proximally by a factor other than RA and repressed distally by FGF8.

routes.reversibility: Conditional by construction - the published allele is already a Cre-conditional in the LPM, so an inducible version is a reagent swap rather than a new design.
routes.lethality_risk: Medium-high; Meis factors are broad organogenesis regulators and the LPM gives rise to much more than limbs. We did not retrieve viability data and will not assert it.
routes.specificity: LPM-restricted rather than limb-restricted - a larger territory than Prx1-Cre.
routes.difficulty: medium-high: a two-gene conditional cross with four floxed alleles plus a driver.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the best published example of DOSE producing a qualitatively different phenotype (agenesis versus posterior-element loss), which is the shape of claim our Lean threshold-interval family is written for. Stating that as a law about a model - monotone activity to ordered element count - and then mutating the law to check Lean rejects the mutants is a real, bounded job, and it proves consistency of our reasoning, not anything about mice. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does the Meis dose series have a measured activity readout, or only allele count? A threshold law needs a continuous variable and allele count is a proxy.

routes.title: Fgf4 + Fgf8 in the AER - remove the ridge's output and limb development fails
routes.mechanism: The AER's job is to make FGFs. Four Fgf genes have AER-specific expression; only Fgf8 is expressed throughout the ridge and earliest. Inactivating Fgf8 alone reduces bud size, delays Shh and gives hypoplasia or aplasia of specific skeletal elements. Inactivating Fgf4 and Fgf8 together in AER cells or their precursors removes the output entirely: the bud has too few progenitors and cells far from the ridge die.
routes.intervention: Conditional inactivation of Fgf8 in limb ectoderm, or Fgf4 and Fgf8 together in AER cells or their precursors, at chosen stages.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Fgf8 alone: substantial reduction in limb-bud size, delayed Shh, misregulated Fgf4, hypoplasia or aplasia of SPECIFIC skeletal elements - a partial, element-selective loss. Both together: 'In the complete absence of both FGF4 and FGF8 activities, limb development fails.' Severity scales with how early the inactivation happens, because the lesion is progenitor number and survival.

evidence.cite: Sun X, Mariani FV & Martin GR 2002, Nature 418:501-8, 'Functions of FGF signalling from the apical ectodermal ridge in limb development'
evidence.finding: 'FGF4 and FGF8 regulate cell number in the nascent limb bud and are required for survival of cells located far from the AER ... In the complete absence of both FGF4 and FGF8 activities, limb development fails.' Inactivation was performed at different stages.

evidence.cite: Lewandoski M, Sun X & Martin GR 2000, Nat Genet 26:460-3, 'Fgf8 signalling from the AER is essential for normal limb development'
evidence.finding: Inactivating Fgf8 in early limb ectoderm 'causes a substantial reduction in limb-bud size, a delay in Shh expression, misregulation of Fgf4 expression, and hypoplasia or aplasia of specific skeletal elements'. Loss of Fgf4, Fgf9 or Fgf17 alone has no effect on limb formation.

evidence.cite: Lu P, Minowada G & Martin GR 2006, Development 133:33-42, 'Increasing Fgf4 expression in the mouse limb bud causes polysyndactyly and rescues the skeletal defects that result from loss of Fgf8 function'
evidence.finding: Expressing Fgf4 in place of Fgf8 rescues all skeletal defects caused by Fgf8 inactivation, so FGF4 can functionally replace FGF8. Raising FGF signalling in a wild-type bud causes postaxial polydactyly and cutaneous syndactyly: 'the importance of controlling the level of FGF gene expression for normal limb development'.

routes.reversibility: Not reversible once progenitors are dead - the lesion is cell number, and lost cells do not come back. This is the clearest case on the page of an irreversible cellular commitment, as opposed to a transcriptional state.
routes.lethality_risk: Low-medium when restricted to limb ectoderm; Fgf8 has major non-limb roles so the driver carries the risk, not the gene.
routes.specificity: Both limbs; element-selective at intermediate doses, which makes it a partial-loss route rather than an all-or-nothing one.
routes.difficulty: medium-high: two floxed genes plus an AER-specific driver, and the stage of inactivation has to be controlled because it sets severity.
routes.what_we_would_run:
This is the one route whose mechanism is explicitly QUANTITATIVE - cell number and survival - and so the one our reaction-diffusion and growth simulators can actually represent. We can simulate bud size as a function of FGF source strength and ask at what point the pattern-forming domain falls below the size that supports digit condensations. That is a simulated result and would be labelled as such; we have no calibration that would let us attach a skeletal count to it.

STUDY: `shh-grem1-fgf-loop` bears on this route: AER-FGF output is the loop's drive term, and Lu et al.'s result that FGF4 fully substitutes for FGF8 says the ODE should carry total FGF dose, not per-gene identity.
open_questions: Lu et al. show FGF4 can replace FGF8 entirely, so AER-FGF identity does not matter but AER-FGF LEVEL does. Any model that scores per-gene rather than per-total-dose will get this wrong.

routes.title: Grem1 - remove the BMP antagonist and the mesenchyme kills itself
routes.mechanism: Mesenchymal GREMLIN1 antagonises BMP, and that antagonism is what permits a functional AER to form and the SHH/FGF feedback loop to propagate. Without it the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback never gets going and the core limb-bud mesenchyme is eliminated by apoptosis - the same fate as the metanephric mesenchyme in the same mutant.
routes.intervention: Grem1 germline null, or conditional deletion in limb mesenchyme.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Failure to establish a functional AER and the SHH/FGF loop; core mesenchyme eliminated by apoptosis. Neonatal lethal from absence of kidneys, with lung septation defects.

evidence.cite: Michos O et al. 2004, Development 131:3401-10, 'Gremlin-mediated BMP antagonism induces the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback signaling controlling metanephric kidney and limb organogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'A Grem1 null mutation in the mouse ... causes neonatal lethality because of the lack of kidneys and lung septation defects. In early limb buds, mesenchymal Grem1 is required to establish a functional apical ectodermal ridge and the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback signaling that propagates the sonic hedgehog morphogen'; the metanephric mesenchyme 'is eliminated by apoptosis, in the same way as the core mesenchymal cells of the limb bud'.

routes.reversibility: None as germline. Apoptotic loss of the mesenchymal core is not recoverable.
routes.lethality_risk: HIGH and certain: neonatal lethal from renal agenesis. Another case where the limb phenotype is never seen in a living adult.
routes.specificity: Poor; the same BMP-antagonism requirement operates in kidney and lung.
routes.difficulty: low to make, not viable.
routes.what_we_would_run:
Grem1 is the inhibitor arm of the self-terminating loop (see tissue-shh-grem1-fgf-loop), so it is the parameter our activator-inhibitor simulators would move first. We can run it; we cannot calibrate it, and we would say so.

STUDY: `shh-grem1-fgf-loop` bears on this route: GREM1 is the loop's inhibitor arm and therefore the first parameter the ODE would move.
open_questions: A limb-mesenchyme-restricted conditional should separate the limb from the kidney phenotype; our search did not retrieve one and we will not assume it exists.

routes.title: Shh null (and why Gli3 shows this is the wrong route)
routes.mechanism: Deleting Shh removes distal limb structures, but it also removes the organiser of the notochord, floor plate, neural tube and axial skeleton, giving cyclopia and loss of the spinal column and most ribs. More importantly, the limb part of the phenotype is PERMISSIVE rather than instructive: disrupting one or both Gli3 alleles in a Shh-null background progressively restores distal limb development and digit formation. SHH's limb role is to counteract GLI3 repression, not to build a limb.
routes.intervention: Shh germline null; Shh;Gli3 double mutants; Gli3 null (extra toes, Xt) alone.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Shh null: absence of distal limb structures, PLUS cyclopia, absence of ventral neural tube cell types, and absence of the spinal column and most ribs. Gli3 null alone: pronounced POLYDACTYLY with loss of digit identity and ectopic anterior Shh - the opposite direction. Shh-/-;Gli3-/-: distal limb development and digits progressively restored.

evidence.cite: Chiang C et al. 1996, Nature 383:407-13, 'Cyclopia and defective axial patterning in mice lacking Sonic hedgehog gene function'
evidence.finding: Shh null: 'absence of distal limb structures, cyclopia, absence of ventral cell types within the neural tube, and absence of the spinal column and most of the ribs', with early defects in notochord and floorplate.

evidence.cite: te Welscher P et al. 2002, Science 298:827-30, 'Progression of vertebrate limb development through SHH-mediated counteraction of GLI3'
evidence.finding: 'the polydactyly of Gli3-deficient mice arises independently of SHH signaling. Disruption of one or both Gli3 alleles in mouse embryos lacking Shh progressively restores limb distal development and digit formation ... SHH signaling counteracts GLI3-mediated repression of key regulator genes, cell survival, and distal progression.'

evidence.cite: Buscher D et al. 1997, Mech Dev 62:175-82, 'Evidence for genetic control of Sonic hedgehog by Gli3 in mouse limb development'
evidence.finding: Shh and Gli3 expression domains are mutually exclusive in the limb bud; in Gli3-null extra toes (Xt) mice Shh is ectopically expressed anteriorly, with Ptc, Fgf, Bmp and Hoxd misexpressed accordingly.

evidence.cite: Hill P, Gotz K & Ruther U 2009, Dev Biol 328:506-16, 'A SHH-independent regulation of Gli3 is a significant determinant of anteroposterior patterning of the limb bud'
evidence.finding: Quantitative demand for GLI3 varies across phases of distal limb formation; unprocessed full-length GLI3 is dispensable for AP patterning and digit identities are most likely defined by GLI3 repressor activity alone; Gli3 is also regulated independently of SHH.

routes.reversibility: None as germline; Shh conditional alleles are the reversible version and are covered under cell-zpa-shh-timing.
routes.lethality_risk: Very high and for reasons unrelated to limbs - cyclopia and axial skeleton loss. Nobody should propose Shh-null as a route to a limbless mouse, and the page should say so explicitly because it is the gene everyone names first.
routes.specificity: Terrible. This is the least limb-specific route in the design space, which is exactly why the ZRS exists as an alternative: the enhancer separates the limb function from all the others.
routes.difficulty: low to make, useless as an animal.
routes.what_we_would_run: Use the Shh/ZRS contrast as the page's central argument: the SAME gene, approached through its coding sequence or through one of its enhancers, gives a dead cyclopic embryo or a viable limb-reduced mouse. That contrast is the strongest single thing we can show a judge about why cis-regulation is the interesting layer. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: The te Welscher result means ZRS-null truncation is a failure to RELIEVE GLI3 repression rather than a failure to deliver a positive signal. Any model of 'enhancer activity to skeletal element count' that treats SHH as an instructive morphogen has the sign of the mechanism wrong, even if it fits the data.

routes.title: p63 - limbs absent or truncated because the AER never differentiates
routes.mechanism: p63 is expressed in the ectodermal surfaces of the limb buds and is required for the AER to differentiate and to be maintained as a stratified epithelium. The lesion is not induction of the limb field and not mesenchymal signalling: it is the failure of a progenitor epithelium to sustain itself. Mice lacking p63 are BORN ALIVE, which makes this the only amelia-class route on this page that is not immediately lethal for a non-limb reason.
routes.intervention: p63 germline knockout (two independent lines, both 1999). A conditional version restricted to limb ectoderm would be the design worth proposing.
routes.predicted_phenotype: 'Their limbs are absent or truncated, defects that are caused by a failure of the apical ectodermal ridge to differentiate' (Mills et al.); limb truncations 'due to a failure to maintain the apical ectodermal ridge' (Yang et al.). Severe accompanying ectodermal phenotype: no skin stratification, absence of all squamous epithelia and their derivatives including hair follicles, teeth, mammary, lacrimal and salivary glands; craniofacial defects.

evidence.cite: Mills AA et al. 1999, Nature 398:708-13, 'p63 is a p53 homologue required for limb and epidermal morphogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'Mice lacking p63 are born alive but have striking developmental defects. Their limbs are absent or truncated, defects that are caused by a failure of the apical ectodermal ridge to differentiate.' Skin lacks stratification; hair follicles, teeth and mammary glands absent.

evidence.cite: Yang A et al. 1999, Nature 398:714-8, 'p63 is essential for regenerative proliferation in limb, craniofacial and epithelial development'
evidence.finding: 'The limb truncations are due to a failure to maintain the apical ectodermal ridge, a stratified epithelium, essential for limb development'; absence of all squamous epithelia and derivatives; p63 maintains the progenitor-cell populations sustaining epithelial morphogenesis.

routes.reversibility: None as germline.
routes.lethality_risk: High in practice. Born alive, but with no stratified skin and no epidermal appendages a pup cannot maintain barrier function; this is a severe phenotype in the welfare sense even though the embryo reaches term. The two papers report birth, not survival.
routes.specificity: Poor as a germline allele - it is an ectodermal phenotype, of which the limb is one part. A limb-ectoderm conditional would in principle fix this and we found no such study.
routes.difficulty: low as germline; medium for the conditional that would actually be worth making.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing computational. p63 earns its place because it is a THIRD mechanism class the existing dossier omits: not induction failure (Fgf10, Wnt3), not signalling-centre output failure (ZRS, Fgf4/8), but failure of the signalling centre's epithelium to differentiate at all. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Why is the phenotype 'absent OR truncated' rather than uniform? Variable expressivity in an amelia-class allele is itself informative and we did not read the bodies to find out.

routes.title: Hand2 - the posterior prepattern, and the gene cetaceans lost
routes.mechanism: HAND2 is a bHLH regulator that establishes anterior and posterior polarity of the nascent limb-bud mesenchyme and sits upstream of SHH. It controls expression of proximal limb genes and sets the Gli3 and Tbx3 expression boundaries that define where the ZPA can form. It functions in dimers with other bHLH factors (TWIST1) in balance with ETS factors, and that balance sets the anterior-posterior pattern.
routes.intervention: Conditional Hand2 deletion in limb mesenchyme; or perturbation of the HAND2/TWIST1/ETV dimerisation balance.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Loss of the posterior prepattern needed for Shh, hence a posteriorly-biased reduction rather than whole-limb loss. We did not retrieve a Hand2 conditional limb skeletal phenotype and will not state one. In the opposite direction, Etv4/Etv5 loss gives preaxial polydactyly which is suppressed by a Hand2 mutation - genetic antagonism, so the node is bidirectional.

evidence.cite: Osterwalder M et al. 2014, Dev Cell 31:345-357, 'HAND2 targets define a network of transcriptional regulators that compartmentalize the early limb bud mesenchyme'
evidence.finding: 'HAND2 controls the expression of genes functioning in the proximal limb bud and orchestrates the establishment of anterior and posterior polarity of the nascent limb bud mesenchyme by impacting Gli3 and Tbx3 expression. TBX3 is required downstream of HAND2 to refine the posterior Gli3 expression boundary.'

evidence.cite: Zhang Z et al. 2010, Development 137:3417-26, 'Preaxial polydactyly: interactions among ETV, TWIST1 and HAND2 control anterior-posterior patterning of the limb'
evidence.finding: Twist1 is required to inhibit anterior Shh; genetic synergism with Etv4/Etv5 via direct TWIST1-ETV association; 'the PPD phenotype observed in Etv mutants is suppressed by a mutation in Hand2, indicative of genetic antagonism'.

evidence.cite: Thewissen JGM et al. 2006, PNAS 103:8414-8, 'Developmental basis for hind-limb loss in dolphins and origin of the cetacean bodyplan'
evidence.finding: In the dolphin hindlimb bud 'Sonic hedgehog (Shh) ... is absent' and 'failure to establish a ZPA is associated with the absence of Hand2, an upstream regulator of Shh'.

routes.reversibility: Conditional alleles exist in the published work; no inducible time-course was retrieved.
routes.lethality_risk: High for germline - HAND2 is required in heart and branchial arches. Limb-restricted conditional is mandatory.
routes.specificity: Limb mesenchyme if conditional; posterior-biased within the limb.
routes.difficulty: medium.
routes.what_we_would_run: Hand2 is the node that links the mouse genetics to the cetacean natural experiment, and the page should draw that line explicitly: whales lost hindlimbs with Hand2 absent from the bud and Shh never established, which is upstream of the ZRS lesion snakes have. Two independent natural limb losses, two different layers of the same network. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Is the dolphin Hand2 absence a cause or a consequence? Thewissen et al. report association, and we are reading an abstract. We would not state causation.

routes.title: Cut the AER off at a chosen hour - the original timing experiment
routes.mechanism: The AER is a physical strip of thickened ectoderm at the distal tip of the bud. Excising it stops distal outgrowth from that moment, and what is already specified proximally still forms. The level of the resulting truncation is therefore a function of WHEN the ridge is removed, which makes this the oldest and most direct demonstration that limb loss is a timing problem rather than only a genetic one.
routes.intervention: Microsurgical excision of the AER from a chick limb bud at a staged time point. In mouse this is not practical in utero; the equivalents are the genetic routes (gene-aer-fgf4-fgf8) or explant culture (invitro-limb-bud-explant).
routes.predicted_phenotype: Progressive distal truncation whose level tracks the stage of excision: earlier removal leaves less limb. The classical series is quantitative.

evidence.cite: Summerbell D 1974, J Embryol Exp Morphol 32:651-60, 'A quantitative analysis of the effect of excision of the AER from the chick limb-bud'
evidence.finding: PubMed record retrieved and the title and MeSH terms (Ectoderm, Extremities, Gestational Age, Humerus, Radius, Ulna, Morphogenesis, Wings) confirm a staged quantitative excision series in chick. NO ABSTRACT IS AVAILABLE in the PubMed record, so we have not read any result statement from this paper and we report only what the record itself shows.

evidence.cite: Lewandoski M, Sun X & Martin GR 2000, Nat Genet 26:460-3
evidence.finding: States the classical premise independently: 'Removal of the AER in chick results in limbs lacking distal skeletal elements' and FGF proteins can substitute for the AER.

routes.reversibility: Not reversible once cut, but FGF protein beads substitute for the removed ridge, which is the sufficiency half of the experiment and makes the manipulation effectively two-way in chick.
routes.lethality_risk: Low in chick; the manipulation is local.
routes.specificity: One limb, one bud, at one time - the most spatially and temporally precise intervention available anywhere in this design space.
routes.difficulty: low in chick (a classical embryology technique), impractical in mouse in utero.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the physical ground truth for the timing axis. Our growth simulators can reproduce 'stop distal outgrowth at time t and see what is already specified', and the chick excision series is the only dataset that could calibrate such a model - except that we cannot read Summerbell's numbers from the PubMed record, so the calibration is not available to us today. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: We could not access the numerical series. Any claim we make about the quantitative relationship between excision stage and truncation level would be unsupported by what we actually read.

routes.title: Kill the AER genetically with a cell-autonomous toxin
routes.mechanism: Instead of cutting the ridge off, express diphtheria toxin A under a promoter active in AER precursors, so the signalling centre is deleted cell-autonomously and without surgery. This is the standard technique for ablating an organiser in the mouse; it has been used to remove the roof plate from the neural tube and to ablate lens precursors before placode formation, both of which produced the expected loss of the structures that depended on the organiser.
routes.intervention: An AER-restricted promoter (for example an Msx2 or limb-ectoderm element) driving attenuated DTA, or a Cre driver crossed to a ROSA26-LoxP-DTA reporter.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED, NOT OBSERVED. By analogy with AER excision the expectation is distal truncation set by the onset of toxin expression, with the proximal skeleton retained. We found NO published AER DTA ablation in our searches and we would not state a phenotype for it.

evidence.cite: Lee KJ, Dietrich P & Jessell TM 2000, Nature 403:734-40, 'Genetic ablation reveals that the roof plate is essential for dorsal interneuron specification'
evidence.finding: A genetic strategy selectively ablated the roof plate in mouse embryos; embryos without a roof plate lack all the interneuron subtypes normally generated in the dorsal third of the neural tube, from loss of non-autonomous signals. Establishes the method for organiser ablation in mouse.

evidence.cite: Zhang Y et al. 2008, Dev Biol 323:53-63, 'Dominant inhibition of lens placode formation in mice'
evidence.finding: Transgenic mice expressing attenuated diphtheria toxin (Tox176) from a modified Pax6 promoter ablated lens precursor cells BEFORE placode formation, allowing the role of the structure to be tested at its earliest stage. Demonstrates that pre-placodal ablation with an attenuated toxin is achievable.

routes.reversibility: None - toxin-killed cells do not return. The control is over WHEN, not whether.
routes.lethality_risk: Depends entirely on promoter leakiness; an attenuated toxin is used precisely to keep ablation local.
routes.specificity: As specific as the promoter. An AER-only driver would be the most limb-specific cellular intervention possible.
routes.difficulty: medium-high, and the honest difficulty is finding a driver that is on in AER precursors and nowhere that matters.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. This route is on the page as a clearly-labelled PROPOSAL, to show the shape of the design space rather than to claim a result. Presenting it as established would be the exact failure mode the page exists to avoid. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does an AER-specific driver with the right onset exist? Our search covered 'diphtheria toxin ablation apical ectodermal ridge genetic mouse' on PubMed and returned four records, none of them an AER ablation. That is the scope of our negative, not a statement about the literature.

routes.title: Remove the ZPA's signal at a chosen stage - digits disappear in a defined order
routes.mechanism: SHH from the ZPA does two separable jobs: a very transient early patterning job that assigns digit identity, and an extended growth-promoting job during which the digit precursor mesenchyme expands and is recruited into condensing digit primordia. Deleting Shh progressively earlier with an inducible Cre removes progressively more digits, and the order in which they are lost mirrors an alternating anterior-posterior sequence of normal digit formation.
routes.intervention: Tamoxifen-inducible Cre (ShhCreER) with a conditional Shh allele, dosed at a chosen embryonic day.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Progressive loss of digits, with the number lost set by how early Shh is removed. Not limb loss: the stylopod and zeugopod are not the target. This route tunes AUTOPOD CONTENT, precisely and reproducibly.

evidence.cite: Zhu J et al. 2008, Dev Cell 14:624-32, 'Uncoupling Sonic hedgehog control of pattern and expansion of the developing limb bud'
evidence.finding: 'Deleting the mouse Shh gene at different times using a conditional Cre line, we find that Shh functions to control limb development in two phases: a very transient, early patterning phase regulating digit identity, and an extended growth-promoting phase ... The progressive loss of digits upon successively earlier Shh removal mirrors this alternating sequence.'

evidence.cite: Scherz PJ et al. 2004, Science 305:396-9, 'The limb bud Shh-Fgf feedback loop is terminated by expansion of former ZPA cells'
evidence.finding: Shh-expressing cells and their descendants cannot express Gremlin; their proliferation forms a physical barrier separating the Shh signal from Gremlin-expressing cells, which breaks the Shh-Fgf4 loop and thereby affects limb size.

routes.reversibility: Reversible in the sense that matters for experimental design: the lesion is applied at a time of the experimenter's choosing, not at fertilisation. It is not reversible after the fact.
routes.lethality_risk: Low when induction is late enough to miss the early Shh requirements in notochord and neural tube - which is exactly the advantage of the inducible allele over the germline null (compare gene-shh-gli3, which is catastrophic).
routes.specificity: Autopod, both limbs, graded.
routes.difficulty: low-medium; the alleles are published and tamoxifen dosing is routine.
routes.what_we_would_run:
This is the best-posed quantitative dataset in the whole design space for our Lean threshold work: an ordered stimulus (induction time) mapping to an ordered, countable outcome (digit number). Stating 'given a monotone map from signal duration to element count, an ordered duration series implies an ordered count series', then mutating the monotonicity and the threshold and showing Lean rejects both mutants, is a bounded job. It proves our reasoning is consistent; it proves nothing about mice, and the page must say that in the same sentence.

STUDY: `shh-grem1-fgf-loop`, the ODE of the maintenance loop, bears on this route: Scherz et al.'s loop termination by expansion of former-ZPA descendants is a termination mechanism the ODE would have to represent, and a model with no spatial term cannot.
open_questions: Scherz et al. make loop termination a consequence of CELL LINEAGE geometry rather than of a transcriptional timer. A model with no spatial representation of former-ZPA descendants cannot express that mechanism at all.

routes.title: Tune the limb by changing how fast the morphogen falls apart
routes.mechanism: FGF10 is an intrinsically unstable protein that unfolds and is rapidly inactivated at 37 C, and the thermodynamic stability of the 22 mammalian FGFs varies widely. Engineered FGF10 variants with a melting temperature more than 19 C above wild type bind receptors, activate signalling and induce gene expression identically in cell assays, yet behave completely differently in tissue - which implies that protein half-life, not receptor affinity, is part of how the limb reads this signal.
routes.intervention: Knock in a stabilised (or, for limb reduction, a destabilised) Fgf10 allele. Stabilised FGF10 variants implanted into chicken limb buds markedly altered limb morphogenesis and inhibited growth of mouse embryonic tibias.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Stabilised direction (measured): suppressed lung branching with increased alveolarisation and epithelial expansion; inhibited embryonic tibia growth; markedly altered limb morphogenesis in chick bud implants. Destabilised direction (PROPOSED, not measured): a graded hypomorphic FGF10 signal, predicted to give partial limb reduction rather than the all-or-nothing amelia of the null.

evidence.cite: Czyrek AA et al. 2025, Cell Mol Life Sci 82:167, 'Increased thermal stability of FGF10 leads to ectopic signaling during development'
evidence.finding: 'FGF10, an important limb and lung morphogen, exists as an intrinsically unstable protein that is prone to unfolding and is rapidly inactivated at 37 C'; STAB variants with +19 C melting temperature were indistinguishable in receptor binding and signalling in cells but 'inhibited the growth of mouse embryonic tibias and markedly altered limb morphogenesis when implanted into chicken limb buds, collectively demonstrating that thermal instability should be considered an important regulator of FGF function that prevents ectopic signaling'.

routes.reversibility: A knock-in allele is not reversible; but recombinant protein delivery is, and the published work is a bead/implant experiment, which is the acute, dose-controlled version.
routes.lethality_risk: Unknown for a destabilised germline allele. If it behaves as a graded Fgf10 hypomorph the lung phenotype scales with it, so the lethality that sinks the Fgf10 null is likely to scale too.
routes.specificity: Poor at the gene level (FGF10 serves many organs) but unusual at the BIOPHYSICAL level: nothing else on this page proposes to tune a phenotype by changing a protein's folding stability rather than its sequence-level function.
routes.difficulty: high, and genuinely novel - we found no published destabilised-FGF10 animal.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the one route where a protein-structure model, rather than a genome model, is the right tool: predict melting temperature for designed FGF10 variants and check against the measured STAB series, which gives a held-out numerical benchmark with real values. We have not run it and have no structure pipeline today. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does a destabilised FGF10 produce a graded limb phenotype, or does the limb buffer ligand half-life entirely? Unknown; the published direction is the stabilising one.

routes.title: Trigger the self-terminating loop early
routes.mechanism: Limb outgrowth is driven by a positive feedback loop between Shh, Gremlin1 and AER-FGFs. The loop is not stopped by an external clock: rising FGF activity itself represses Grem1, so the circuit is self-promoting AND self-terminating. Independently, the descendants of former Shh-expressing cells cannot express Gremlin and physically interpose between the Shh source and the Gremlin domain, breaking the loop geometrically. Either mechanism, triggered early, should stop outgrowth early.
routes.intervention: Raise FGF activity in the early bud to engage the Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop before the limb has grown (a conditional Fgf4 gain-of-function allele exists and is known to raise FGF signalling in the bud); or force premature expansion of the former-ZPA lineage.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED for the deliberate-early-termination direction. The components are measured: compound mutants defective in the positive loop show that FGF signalling represses Grem1 in a manner dependent on high FGF activity, in both mouse and chick. Note that the one published high-FGF4 gain-of-function gave postaxial POLYDACTYLY and syndactyly, not truncation - so 'more FGF' is not simply 'earlier stop', and we would not assert the predicted direction.

evidence.cite: Verheyden JM & Sun X 2008, Nature 454:638-41, 'An Fgf/Gremlin inhibitory feedback loop triggers termination of limb bud outgrowth'
evidence.finding: 'genetic evidence that FGF signalling can repress Grem1 expression, revealing a novel Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop ... dependent on high FGF activity ... the positive Fgf/Shh loop drives outgrowth and an increase in FGF signalling, which triggers the Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop ... a self-promoting and self-terminating circuit'.

evidence.cite: Scherz PJ et al. 2004, Science 305:396-9
evidence.finding: Proliferation of former-ZPA descendants 'forms a barrier separating the Shh signal from Gremlin-expressing cells, which breaks down the Shh-Fgf4 loop and thereby affects limb size'.

evidence.cite: Lu P, Minowada G & Martin GR 2006, Development 133:33-42
evidence.finding: A conditional Fgf4 gain-of-function allele activated in a wild-type limb bud 'causes formation of a supernumerary posterior digit (postaxial polydactyly), as well as cutaneous syndactyly between all the digits'.

routes.reversibility: In principle fully reversible, because the target is a dynamic circuit state rather than a genomic lesion - but no published experiment turns the loop off and back on.
routes.lethality_risk: Low if limb-restricted.
routes.specificity: Both limbs; the loop is limb-bud-specific in its Shh/Grem1 arm.
routes.difficulty: high. The circuit is the thing everyone understands least well in quantitative terms, which is why 'trigger it early' is a sentence and not a protocol.
routes.what_we_would_run:
This is the one route our existing reaction-diffusion and pattern simulators represent natively: an activator-inhibitor system with delayed negative feedback. We can run it and show how termination time moves with the inhibitory-loop gain. We CANNOT calibrate it - we have no registered calibration anywhere in our system - so the output is a simulated trajectory labelled 'simulated, not observed', and the bridge from it to a skeletal element count is exactly the kind our coupling layer refuses.

STUDY: `shh-grem1-fgf-loop` IS this route: the ODE is the model of exactly this circuit, and the route is the biology it claims to represent.
open_questions: Mouse and chick terminate the loop in a different SEQUENCE, which is what led Verheyden & Sun to the inhibitory loop in the first place. A single model fitted to one species is not transferable to the other without saying so.

routes.title: Detune the digit-patterning Turing network
routes.mechanism: Digits emerge from undifferentiated mesenchyme through a self-organising periodic mechanism. Combined experiment and modelling implicate a Turing network implemented by BMP, SOX9 and WNT, modulated by morphogen gradients; a two-dimensional simulation of this network reproduces wild-type and perturbed Sox9 expression patterns. Changing the network's parameters changes the periodic pattern, and in principle a sufficiently detuned network produces no periodic skeletal pattern at all.
routes.intervention: Pharmacological or genetic modulation of BMP and WNT in the autopod field, guided by the published model.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Changes in DIGIT PATTERN - number, spacing, thickness. NOT limb loss. This route is in the design space because it is the mechanism that decides what the autopod looks like, and because it is the only route here with a published, runnable, quantitative model attached. Claiming it produces a limbless mouse would be unsupported.

evidence.cite: Raspopovic J, Marcon L, Russo L & Sharpe J 2014, Science 345:566-70, 'Digit patterning is controlled by a Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing network modulated by morphogen gradients'
evidence.finding: 'By combining experiments and modeling, we reveal evidence that a Turing network implemented by Bmp, Sox9, and Wnt drives digit specification. We develop a realistic two-dimensional simulation of digit patterning and show that this network, when modulated by morphogen gradients, recapitulates the expression patterns of Sox9 in the wild type and in perturbation experiments.'

routes.reversibility: Pharmacological modulation is acutely reversible in explant; genetic modulation is not.
routes.lethality_risk: BMP and WNT are systemic; any whole-animal manipulation is dangerous and any explant manipulation is not an animal.
routes.specificity: Autopod pattern only.
routes.difficulty: medium in explant, high in vivo.
routes.what_we_would_run:
We have 12 tissue-scale and 4 developmental-scale reaction-diffusion runs recorded, each with a manifest, numerical checks, input hashes and a verified figure, each labelled simulated-not-observed. Re-instantiating that machinery on the published BMP-SOX9-WNT network is the single most direct reuse of what we already have. It would produce a simulated digit pattern, not a prediction about a mouse.

STUDY: `digit-turing`, the BMP-SOX9-WNT reaction-diffusion model, IS this route: the published network and the model on this page are the same object.
open_questions: A Turing model explains how digits are SPACED. Nothing in it explains why a limb bud exists. Conflating the two is the most likely way a cross-scale system gets this subject wrong, and the page should say so.

routes.title: Use Hox dose to set the wavelength of the digit pattern
routes.mechanism: Progressive removal of Hoxa13 and Hoxd11-Hoxd13 from a Gli3-null background produces progressively more severe polydactyly with thinner, more densely packed digits. Read through a Turing framework, distal Hox dose modulates the period, or wavelength, of the digit/non-digit pattern. The resemblance of the extreme phenotype to fish fin endoskeleton suggests the pentadactyl state is a modified ancestral version of the same mechanism.
routes.intervention: Graded removal of distal Hox genes, on a Gli3-null background, as published.
routes.predicted_phenotype: MORE digits, thinner and more densely packed, as distal Hox dose falls - the opposite of limb reduction. Included because it is the only published, dose-resolved control knob on a limb pattern-forming mechanism, and because it defines what the pattern-level knob actually does.

evidence.cite: Sheth R et al. 2012, Science 338:1476-80, 'Hox genes regulate digit patterning by controlling the wavelength of a Turing-type mechanism'
evidence.finding: 'the progressive reduction in Hoxa13 and Hoxd11-Hoxd13 genes ... from the Gli3-null background results in progressively more severe polydactyly, displaying thinner and densely packed digits. Combined with computer modeling, our results argue for a Turing-type mechanism underlying digit patterning, in which the dose of distal Hox genes modulates the digit period or wavelength.'

routes.reversibility: None; germline allelic series.
routes.lethality_risk: Not retrieved; the compound mutants are described as analysed, not as viable adults, and we will not assert either.
routes.specificity: Autopod.
routes.difficulty: high - this is a large multi-allele breeding programme.
routes.what_we_would_run:
Sheth et al. give an ordered dose mapped to an ordered wavelength, which is a second, independent instance of the same claim shape as the ZRS series and the Shh timing series. Three independent ordered-dose datasets in one subject is unusual, and it is the honest reason to call limb development a good benchmark domain - not because we can predict it, but because it is unusually well ordered.

STUDY: `digit-turing` bears on this route: distal Hox dose is the published wavelength parameter of that model, and Sheth et al.'s allelic series is the only measured dose-to-wavelength data the model could be checked against.
open_questions: Does wavelength modulation ever reach a regime with ZERO digits, or does the pattern simply get finer until the field runs out? The published direction goes the other way and we have no evidence for the zero limit.

routes.title: Tamoxifen-inducible Cre - choose the hour the gene goes away
routes.mechanism: A CreER fusion sits inactive in the cytoplasm until tamoxifen is given, at which point it enters the nucleus and recombines a floxed allele. The same genetic lesion applied at different embryonic days produces different phenotypes, because developmental requirements are windowed. This converts a binary genotype into a one-dimensional experimental variable.
routes.intervention: A floxed allele of the target gene crossed to an appropriate CreER driver, with tamoxifen dosed at a chosen embryonic day.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Set by the target and the time. Two measured examples: ShhCreER removal progressively earlier removes progressively more digits; Tbx4 ablation before hindlimb-field expression blocks outgrowth, shortly after onset gives proximal hypoplasia with normal outgrowth and normal Fgf10, and later gives NO limb defect at all.

evidence.cite: Zhu J et al. 2008, Dev Cell 14:624-32
evidence.finding: Conditional Cre deletion of Shh at different times separates a transient early patterning phase from an extended growth phase; progressively earlier removal gives progressive digit loss.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2007, Development 134:93-103
evidence.finding: 'Loss of Tbx4 during later limb outgrowth produces no limb defects, revealing a brief developmental requirement for Tbx4 function.'

routes.reversibility: The DECISION is reversible up to the moment of dosing; the recombination is not. This is control over onset, not an on/off switch.
routes.lethality_risk: This is the mechanism that REMOVES lethality risk, by letting the gene do its early non-limb jobs before being deleted. It is the reason Shh can be studied in the limb at all without cyclopia.
routes.specificity: Temporal; spatial specificity comes from the driver, not from the inducibility.
routes.difficulty: low-medium. Standard, well-characterised, widely available reagents.
routes.what_we_would_run: Encode in the coupling layer that a genotype-to-phenotype claim with no time index is not composable. Naiche's three-outcomes-from-one-lesion is the anchoring example and it is a one-record change. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Tamoxifen itself affects pregnancy and embryonic development; the published designs handle this, but any new stage series needs vehicle controls.

routes.title: Prx1-Cre - confine the lesion to limb-bud mesenchyme
routes.mechanism: A Prx1 (Prrx1) limb enhancer drives Cre throughout early limb-bud mesenchyme, with recombination first detectable at E9.5 and essentially complete in all limb mesenchymal cells by E10.5, plus a subset of craniofacial mesenchyme. Cre is NEVER detected in limb-bud ectoderm. So a floxed gene can be removed from the limb mesenchyme and left intact in lung, kidney, heart and allantois.
routes.intervention: Cross any floxed allele to Prx1-Cre. For an inducible version, Prx1-CreER.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Target-dependent, but the decisive property is what it AVOIDS: the lung agenesis that kills Fgf10 nulls, the renal agenesis that kills Grem1 nulls, the allantoic failure that kills Tbx4 nulls, and the cardiac defects of Tbx5 nulls are all outside the Prx1 domain.

evidence.cite: Logan M et al. 2002, Genesis 33:77-80, 'Expression of Cre Recombinase in the developing mouse limb bud driven by a Prxl enhancer'
evidence.finding: 'recombinase activity is first observed in the earliest limb bud at 9.5 dpc. By early to mid bud stages at 10.5 dpc recombination is essentially complete in all mesenchymal cells in the limb. Expression of the Cre recombinase was never detected in the limb bud ectoderm.' Also a subset of craniofacial mesenchyme.

routes.reversibility: None - constitutive Cre. The CreER version adds the time axis.
routes.lethality_risk: This is the single most important lethality-reducing reagent in the design space, and the reason a viable limb-reduced mouse is reachable by routes whose germline nulls are not.
routes.specificity: Limb MESENCHYME only. It does not reach the AER, so ectoderm-acting targets (Wnt3, beta-catenin, p63, AER-FGFs) need a different driver. The craniofacial subset is a real caveat.
routes.difficulty: low. One of the most widely used drivers in skeletal biology.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing computational. This route is the page's answer to 'how do you get a limbless mouse that is alive', and it is a reagent, not an idea. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: The craniofacial mesenchyme domain means any Prx1-Cre phenotype needs skull assessment before being called limb-specific.

routes.title: Degron knock-in - remove the PROTEIN in hours, not the gene
routes.mechanism: A degron tag (FKBP12-F36V / dTAG) knocked into the endogenous locus leaves the protein normal until a small molecule is given, at which point the ligase machinery degrades it within hours. Unlike Cre, the depletion is post-translational, far faster than protein turnover after gene deletion, and in some systems washable. This is the only route on this page that could in principle switch a limb signal OFF AND BACK ON inside a single embryonic day.
routes.intervention: Knock a dTAG degron into Fgf10, Tbx5, Shh or Grem1 by zygote editing, then dose the dam with the dTAG ligand at a chosen hour.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED for limb genes. What IS measured is the method: in a homozygous FKBP12-F36V knock-in at Nelfb, dTAG depletion was 'non-toxic, rapid, and efficient in embryos from the zygote-to-mid-gestation stages' irrespective of administration route, and acute depletion revealed a stage-specific requirement invisible to a constitutive knockout. No limb gene has been degron-tagged in published work that we found.

evidence.cite: Abuhashem A, Lee AS, Joyner AL & Hadjantonakis AK 2022, Dev Cell 57:1068-1080.e6, 'Rapid and efficient degradation of endogenous proteins in vivo identifies stage-specific roles of RNA Pol II pausing in mammalian development'
evidence.finding: A homozygous FKBP12-F36V knock-in mouse at Nelfb; 'irrespective of the route of administration the dTAG system is non-toxic, rapid, and efficient in embryos from the zygote-to-mid-gestation stages'. Acute depletion revealed a specific role in zygote-to-2-cell development.

evidence.cite: Antczak W et al. 2026, Commun Biol 9(1), 'Degron models: a toolbox for rapid in vivo depletion of essential proteins regulating mRNA metabolism'
evidence.finding: Seven degron-tag mouse models by direct zygote editing. 'Degron tags occasionally cause phenotypes that can be mitigated by tag position or tagging system change. In cells, both approaches yield rapid and sustained degradation. In mice, dTAG depletion is effective but varies by protein and administration route, whereas BromoTag shows no in vivo activity.'

routes.reversibility: The highest of any route here IN PRINCIPLE - ligand washout should restore protein. Whether a limb bud recovers after a transient depletion is an empirical question nobody has asked, and it is the most interesting unasked question on this page.
routes.lethality_risk: Low by design: the protein is present for every requirement outside the chosen window.
routes.specificity: Temporal and protein-level; NOT spatial. The ligand reaches the whole embryo, so a degron depletes the target everywhere at once. Pairing it with a tissue-restricted system is not solved.
routes.difficulty: high but decreasing. The honest caveats are in the second paper: tags sometimes cause phenotypes on their own, efficiency varies by protein and route, and one of the two tagging systems showed no in vivo activity at all.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. This is a clearly-labelled proposal and belongs on the page as the frontier method rather than as a result. It is also the most likely answer if a modern reviewer asks 'why would you make a germline mutant at all'. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does transient depletion of a limb signal give a REVERSIBLE limb defect, a permanent one, or none? Unknown, and it is the experiment that would most change how this subject is taught.
Degron depletion is systemic. Combining acute temporal control with limb-restricted delivery is an open engineering problem.

routes.title: RECOMMENDED: limb-restricted, stage-selected Fgf10 removal
routes.mechanism: Take the lesion with the strongest, most unambiguous limb phenotype in the literature - loss of FGF10, which abolishes AER formation and so abolishes the limb - and apply it only where and only when you want it. Prx1-CreER restricts recombination to limb-bud mesenchyme, where FGF10 is actually made, and the tamoxifen dose sets the hour. Everything that kills the germline Fgf10 null (lung, thyroid, pituitary, salivary gland) lies outside the Prx1 domain and outside the induction window.
routes.intervention: Fgf10 conditional (floxed) allele crossed to Prx1-CreER. Tamoxifen at a chosen day. Forelimb-restricted and hindlimb-restricted variants can be approached instead through Tbx5-conditional (forelimb) or Tbx4-conditional (hindlimb) alleles if a single-pair phenotype is wanted.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED. We did not find a published Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox limb series and will not state its phenotype. The components are each measured: Fgf10 loss abolishes AER formation and gives absent limbs; Prx1-Cre recombines all limb mesenchyme by E10.5 and never the ectoderm; CreER timing converts a fixed lesion into a stage series. The honest claim is that this is the best-supported DESIGN, not a known result.

evidence.cite: Min H et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:3156-61
evidence.finding: Fgf10 loss abolishes limb bud initiation and gives complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs; Fgf10 is necessary for AER formation and acts upstream of Fgf8. Perinatal lethality is from absent lungs, a defect in a tissue outside the Prx1 domain.

evidence.cite: Logan M et al. 2002, Genesis 33:77-80
evidence.finding: Prx1 limb enhancer drives Cre throughout early limb-bud mesenchyme from E9.5, complete by E10.5, never in limb-bud ectoderm.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2007, Development 134:93-103
evidence.finding: Demonstrates for Tbx4 that the same conditional lesion applied at three different times gives three different outcomes, including none - the general principle this design depends on.

routes.reversibility: Onset is chosen; the recombination is permanent. For true reversibility the degron route is the only candidate.
routes.lethality_risk: LOW, and this is the entire point. The germline Fgf10 null is perinatally lethal from lung agenesis; a Prx1-restricted deletion should not touch the lung. We say 'should' because we found no published viability data for this exact cross.
routes.specificity: Limb mesenchyme, both pairs, with a craniofacial caveat from the driver. A single-pair version (Tbx5 for forelimb, Tbx4 for hindlimb) is substantially more likely to give a viable adult.
routes.difficulty: medium. Every component is an existing, published reagent; the work is breeding, dosing and skeletal analysis, not invention.
routes.what_we_would_run: Before any animal: score the predicted severity ordering across induction times with our pattern simulators, pre-register it, and state explicitly that the simulation is not calibrated and the prediction is a hypothesis. We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm; the proposal is a design, and we would present it as one. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does a Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox animal survive to adulthood? Unknown to us.

Is mesenchymal Fgf10 deletion after E10.5 sufficient to remove a limb, or has the AER already become self-sustaining? The Barrow beta-catenin result shows an existing AER CAN be made to disappear, but that was an ectodermal manipulation, not a mesenchymal one.

routes.title: Snakes - progressive enhancer decay, and a bud that is still there
routes.mechanism: Snake limb loss is not one event. In basal snakes (boa, python) the ZRS is ~80% identical to limbed lizards and still has detectable ZPA activity in boa; in advanced snakes the substitution rate jumps and ZPA activity is gone; in corn snake no ZRS sequence was detected at all. Crucially the python hindlimb bud still initiates, and its HOXD digit enhancers are conserved - the bud reaches a distal phase with transient pre-chondrogenic condensations of tibia, fibula and footplate before arresting.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention - nature's. The engineering lesson is that limb loss was achieved in stages, and that the cis-regulatory decay appears to have STARTED WITH OR AFTER other disruptive events, not before them.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Advanced snakes: complete absence of all skeletal limb structures. Basal snakes: vestigial pelvic girdle and rudimentary hindlimbs. Python embryo: hindlimb development arrests; apical-ridge and polarizing-region signalling pathways are not activated; SHH is weak and transient.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11
evidence.finding: Advanced-snake ZRS shows a substantially increased substitution rate; ZRS from rattlesnake and cobra 'completely lost ZPA-specific activity'; only boa retained ZPA activity; 'The only snake genome in which no ZRS sequence was detected belonged to the corn snake.' And: 'we do not expect that the reintroduction of a fully functional ZRS into a snake genome alone would be sufficient to induce the formation of fully or even partially developed limbs in snakes.'

evidence.cite: Cohn MJ & Tickle C 1999, Nature 399:474-9, 'Developmental basis of limblessness and axial patterning in snakes'
evidence.finding: 'Hindlimb buds are initiated, but apical-ridge and polarizing-region signalling pathways that are normally required for limb development are not activated. Leg bud outgrowth and signalling by Sonic hedgehog in pythons can be rescued by application of fibroblast growth factor or by recombination with chick apical ridge.' Hox expression domains are expanded along the body axis, accounting for forelimb absence and thoracic expansion.

evidence.cite: Leal F & Cohn MJ 2016, Curr Biol 26:2966-73, 'Loss and Re-emergence of Legs in Snakes by Modular Evolution of Sonic hedgehog and HOXD Enhancers'
evidence.finding: 'hindlimb development arrests in python embryos as a result of mutations that abolish essential transcription factor binding sites in the limb-specific enhancer of Sonic hedgehog (SHH). Consequently, SHH transcription is weak and transient'. HOXD digit enhancers are conserved; buds form transitory pre-chondrogenic condensations of tibia, fibula and footplate.

routes.reversibility: The most important negative result in the whole design space: Cohn & Tickle showed python leg bud outgrowth and SHH signalling CAN be rescued by an FGF bead or a chick apical ridge - so the mesenchyme is still competent. But Kvon et al. explicitly expect that restoring the ZRS alone would NOT restore limbs in a snake, because other changes must also have occurred. Rescuable in an embryo manipulation; not rescuable by one genomic edit.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable.
routes.specificity: Whole-lineage; forelimb loss in snakes is attributed to expanded axial Hox domains, a different mechanism from the hindlimb ZRS lesion. Two mechanisms in one animal.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable; this is comparative evidence.
routes.what_we_would_run:
The ZRS ortholog series across 16 species IS the benchmark dataset, and it is the one piece of this subject that maps directly onto what a genome language model emits a score for. We have not scored it.

STUDY: `zrs-conservation` bears on this route: the 16-species ZRS reporter panel and the four ortholog knock-ins are what turn 'snakes lost their limbs' into a graded, scoreable dataset.
open_questions: Forelimb loss (Hox-mediated) and hindlimb reduction (ZRS-mediated) are different mechanisms in the same animal. Any single-locus account of 'the gene for snake limblessness' is incomplete by the field's own statement.

routes.title: Limb-reduced lizards - the knob is how LONG SHH is on, and the losses are not all the same
routes.mechanism: In the Australian skink genus Hemiergis, closely related populations differ in digit number, and evolutionary digit loss is NOT a simple truncation of a pentadactyl programme. The duration of embryonic SHH expression is shortened in limbs with fewer digits, correlating with decreased posterior cell proliferation. Expression of MSX and Distal-less proteins is similar between populations, so the change is specific rather than a general developmental slowdown.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention. The engineering translation is the Shh-duration knob, which in mouse is exactly the ShhCreER timing route.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Graded digit reduction tracking SHH duration. Different squamate clades reduce differently: in Brachymeles, digit-number variation suggests a more labile Digit V than Digit I, contrary to Morse's law and different from Lerista, Hemiergis and Carlia - 'the first evidence of clade-specific modes of digit reduction'.

evidence.cite: Shapiro MD, Hanken J & Rosenthal N 2003, J Exp Zool B 297:48-56, 'Developmental basis of evolutionary digit loss in the Australian lizard Hemiergis'
evidence.finding: 'the duration of embryonic expression of the patterning molecule Sonic hedgehog (SHH) is shortened in limbs with reduced numbers of digits, and is correlated with decreased cell proliferation in the posterior aspect of the limb ... expression of MSX and Distal-less proteins were similar among embryos from different populations.'

evidence.cite: Wagner GP et al. 2018, J Morphol 279:1104-1119, 'Are there general laws for digit evolution in squamates? The loss and re-evolution of digits in a clade of fossorial lizards (Brachymeles, Scincinae)'
evidence.finding: Strong statistical support for digit, but not limb, re-evolution in Brachymeles. 'Digit number variation suggests a more labile Digit V than Digit I, contrary to Morse's law. The observed pattern of digit variation is different from that of other scincid lizards (Lerista, Hemiergis, Carlia) ... the first evidence of clade-specific modes of digit reduction.'

evidence.cite: Rabosky DL et al. 2014, Syst Biol 63:610-27, 'Analysis and visualization of complex macroevolutionary dynamics: an example from Australian scincid lizards'
evidence.finding: 'The Lerista clade is characterized by relatively high lability of body form and has undergone repeated instances of limb reduction.'

evidence.cite: Camaiti M et al. 2024, Proc Biol Sci 291:20241653, 'Patterns of girdle shape and their correlates in Australian limb-reduced skinks'
evidence.finding: Geometric morphometrics across 90 limb-reduced skink species and limbed relatives: clavicle shape converges on an acute anterior bend when forelimbs are lost but hindlimbs retained; coracoid and pelvis simplify as undulation replaces limbed locomotion; girdle integration decreases in taxa lacking forelimb but not hindlimb elements.

routes.reversibility: Wagner et al. report statistical support for DIGIT re-evolution but not limb re-evolution in Brachymeles - the clearest comparative statement available on whether this is reversible on evolutionary timescales.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable.
routes.specificity: Clade-specific, and that is the finding: there is no single squamate mechanism of limb reduction.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. This route is on the page to refute the framing that there is 'a' mechanism for limb loss. Four independent squamate radiations reduce limbs by at least partly different routes, and that is the empirical case for presenting a DESIGN SPACE rather than an answer. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: We found NO molecular (sequence or expression) mechanism published for Lerista limb reduction - the most-cited example of repeated limb loss. Our searches covered 'Lerista limb reduction skink evolution' on PubMed and returned four records, all taxonomic, morphometric or macroevolutionary. That is the scope of our negative; we did not search non-English sources, theses, or preprint servers.

The Camaiti girdle result raises a question we cannot answer: is the converged clavicle shape a locomotor adaptation or a developmental consequence of forelimb loss? The authors give both as possibilities.

routes.title: Whales and dolphins - the bud forms, the AER forms, and then nothing maintains it
routes.mechanism: Cetacean embryos DO initiate hindlimb buds; in dolphins the bud arrests and degenerates around the fifth gestational week. The hindlimb bud forms an AER and expresses Fgf8 initially, but neither the AER nor Fgf8 expression is maintained. SHH is absent from the bud, and the failure to establish a ZPA is associated with absence of HAND2, an upstream regulator of SHH. Separately, cetacean ZRS reporter activity is significantly lower than mouse, consistent with cessation of hindlimb-bud SHH.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention. The translated design is a maintenance failure, not an induction failure - the mouse analogue is beta-catenin removal after AER induction, or late AER-FGF inactivation.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Complete hindlimb loss in the adult; a transient, arrested bud in the embryo. Thewissen et al. interpret the fossil and developmental records together: reduction of SHH expression around 41 Ma led to loss of distal elements, and total loss of SHH expression near the origin of the modern suborders around 34 Ma accounts for further loss - with hindlimb SIZE reduced earlier by gradual microevolutionary change, long before the developmental genes changed.

evidence.cite: Thewissen JGM et al. 2006, PNAS 103:8414-8
evidence.finding: 'In dolphins, the bud arrests and degenerates around the fifth gestational week ... the cetacean hind-limb bud forms an AER and ... this structure expresses Fgf8 initially, but ... neither the AER nor Fgf8 expression is maintained. Moreover, Sonic hedgehog (Shh) ... is absent ... failure to establish a ZPA is associated with the absence of Hand2.' 'Long after locomotor function was totally lost, modulation of developmental control genes eliminated most of the hind-limb skeleton.'

evidence.cite: Sun L et al. 2022, BMC Genomics 23:797, 'Evolutionary genetics of flipper forelimb and hindlimb loss from limb development-related genes in cetaceans'
evidence.finding: 'the regulatory activity of the SHH gene enhancer-ZRS in cetaceans-was significantly lower than in mice, which is consistent with the cessation of SHH gene expression in the hindlimb bud'; accelerated evolution of TBX5 on ancestral cetacean branches; a parallel/convergent FGF10 site (D42G) and a rapidly evolving GREM1 CNE in marine mammals.

evidence.cite: Gavazzi LM et al. 2024, Dev Dyn 253:859-874, 'Protein signaling and morphological development of the tail fluke in the embryonic beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas)'
evidence.finding: In a beluga embryo, immunohistochemistry showed epidermal WNT and FGF signals and mesenchymal/epidermal SHH and GREMLIN in the developing tail fluke, 'most consistent with vertebrate limb development' - i.e. the limb programme was redeployed in a novel appendage after the hindlimb was lost. Single case study; authors state further work is required.

routes.reversibility: Not applicable, but the beluga fluke result is the striking counterpoint: the limb-outgrowth signalling programme was not lost from the genome, it was redeployed elsewhere in the body.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable.
routes.specificity: Hindlimb only - forelimbs became flippers with webbed digits and hyperphalangy, a gain-of-structure change in the same animal.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable.
routes.what_we_would_run:
Nothing, but this is the strongest comparative argument for the MAINTENANCE class of routes: the one natural limb loss where we know the AER formed and then failed is also the one where loss is complete. If you want a limbless animal rather than a truncated one, removing maintenance may beat blocking induction.

STUDY: `zrs-conservation` bears on this route only partially: dolphin is one of the 16 species in the ZRS reporter panel, where its ortholog was active in the ZPA but with activity expanded anteriorly. No cetacean ZRS was taken to knock-in, so there is no phenotype rung for it.
open_questions: Thewissen et al. report an ASSOCIATION between absent HAND2 and failure to establish a ZPA. We read the abstract; we would not restate it as causation.
The 41 Ma and 34 Ma dates are the authors' integration of fossil and developmental data, i.e. their inference, not a measurement.

routes.title: Stickleback pelvic loss - the cleanest natural proof that cis-regulation is the viable route
routes.mechanism: Threespine stickleback populations have repeatedly lost the pelvic apparatus, the hindlimb homologue, through deletion of a tissue-specific Pitx1 enhancer. The same gene's null allele is lethal in laboratory animals. So evolution reached the phenotype by removing the gene's expression in one tissue rather than removing the gene - the same logic as the ZRS, in an independent lineage and a different gene.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention. It is the design precedent that the whole cis-regulatory half of this page rests on.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Pelvic (hindlimb-homologue) reduction or loss, viable, with molecular signatures of positive selection in pelvic-reduced populations.

evidence.cite: Chan YF et al. 2010, Science 327:302-5
evidence.finding: 'Pelvic loss in different natural populations of threespine stickleback fish has occurred through regulatory mutations deleting a tissue-specific enhancer of the Pituitary homeobox transcription factor 1 (Pitx1) gene. The high prevalence of deletion mutations at Pitx1 may be influenced by inherent structural features of the locus. Although Pitx1 null mutations are lethal in laboratory animals, Pitx1 regulatory mutations show molecular signatures of positive selection in pelvic-reduced populations.'

routes.reversibility: Recurrent in both directions across populations; the locus's structural fragility makes the deletion repeatable, which is itself the mechanism of the repeatability.
routes.lethality_risk: None - these are wild, reproducing fish.
routes.specificity: Pelvis only.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable.
routes.what_we_would_run: Two independent natural experiments (stickleback Pitx1, snake ZRS) converge on the same engineering principle: to remove an appendage without killing the animal, delete a tissue-specific enhancer, not the gene. That principle is the page's single transferable conclusion, and it is supported by evidence from two phyla rather than by our opinion. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does the equivalent mouse Pitx1 hindlimb enhancer exist and is it single or redundant? See mol-pitx1-hindlimb-enhancer; unknown to us.

routes.title: Budoids - mESC-derived 3D organoids containing AER-like, surface-ectoderm and limb-mesoderm cells
routes.mechanism: Mouse embryonic stem cells are driven by a 7-day small-molecule protocol into heterogeneous 2D cultures containing cells with limb-bud mesoderm, surface ectoderm and AER properties; dissociating and reaggregating them in low-attachment plates forms free-floating organoids ('budoids') with limb-bud-like features that undergo chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking and elongation within 5 days. The AER-like cells support nearby limb mesoderm and fibroblast identities and enhance tissue polarisation permitting distant cartilage formation - that is, the signalling centre's role in cell fate AND spatial organisation can be dissected without an embryo.
routes.intervention: Make budoids from mESCs carrying the lesion of interest (Fgf10, Tbx5, Shh/ZRS, Grem1, p63), or apply the lesion acutely in culture, and read out AER-like cell specification, mesoderm identity and chondrogenic symmetry breaking.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Readouts are cell-fate proportions, polarisation and cartilage formation - not a skeleton. A budoid cannot tell you whether a mouse has an autopod; it can tell you whether AER-like cells arise and whether the mesoderm responds. That is a genuine but much narrower claim, and the page should not let it be read as a limb.

evidence.cite: Skoufa E et al. 2025, Sci Adv 11(48):eady7682, 'Specialized signaling centers direct cell fate and spatial organization in a mesodermal organoid model'
evidence.finding: 'we developed mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC)-based heterogeneous cultures and a three-dimensional (3D) organoid model, termed budoids, comprising cells with AER, surface ectoderm, and mesoderm properties ... exhibiting chondrogenesis-based symmetry breaking and elongation ... AER-like cells support nearby limb mesoderm and fibroblast identities while enhancing tissue polarization that permits distant cartilage formation.'

evidence.cite: Hu K & Aztekin C 2026, Bio Protoc 16(17):e5808, 'Generation of Budoids: 3D Multilineage Limb Models From Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells'
evidence.finding: A 7-day mESC differentiation protocol; budoids undergo chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking and elongation within 5 days; 'Highly scalable protocol, per differentiation experiment yielding > 9 x 10^[n] cells, sufficient for generating >1,000 budoids.' Adaptable for drug testing and congenital disorder modelling.

routes.reversibility: Fully reversible and fully repeatable - it is cell culture. Conditions can be changed mid-experiment and the experiment can be run a thousand times in parallel.
routes.lethality_risk: None. No animal.
routes.specificity: Limb-bud-like cell types specifically; no systemic physiology at all, which is both the advantage and the limit.
routes.difficulty: medium. A published step-by-step protocol exists, the reagents are small molecules, and the scale is >1,000 budoids per differentiation.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the route a modern reviewer asks for first and it is the only one on this page we could actually execute without an animal facility. It is also where our cross-scale coupling layer has something concrete to refuse: 'AER-like cell proportion in a budoid' to 'skeletal element present in a mouse' is a scale change, a context change and an organism-to-culture change with no registered calibration. We have ZERO registered calibrations today, so that bridge is refused by construction, and saying so is a result about our system rather than about limbs. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Do budoids form a real AER with the stratified epithelium p63 maintains, or AER-LIKE cells by marker expression? The abstract says 'AER properties'; we read an abstract, and the distinction decides what a p63 experiment in budoids would mean.
Budoids break symmetry via chondrogenesis. Whether that is the same symmetry breaking as proximodistal limb outgrowth is not established in what we read.

routes.title: Human iPSC-derived expandable PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchymal cells
routes.mechanism: A defined, xeno-free protocol with a PRRX1-tdTomato reporter selectively induces expandable limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells from human pluripotent stem cells. They proliferate stably through serial passage while retaining chondrogenic potential, and chondrogenic competence tracks PRRX1 expression level. PRRX1 is the same gene whose limb enhancer drives Prx1-Cre in the mouse, so the human in-vitro system and the mouse in-vivo system are anchored on the same marker.
routes.intervention: Derive ExpLBM cells from iPSCs carrying a patient or engineered limb-malformation genotype, expand, and assay chondrogenic differentiation. The authors did exactly this for type II collagenopathy.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Chondrogenic capacity and hyaline cartilaginous tissue formation - a cell-intrinsic readout. It is a HUMAN system, which matters given that this page has two documented human-mouse discordances (CTCF/acheiropodia and WNT3 viability).

evidence.cite: Yamada D et al. 2021, Nat Biomed Eng 5:926-940, 'Induction and expansion of human PRRX1+ limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells from pluripotent stem cells'
evidence.finding: A protocol leveraging PRRX1-tdTomato reporter hPSCs for 'selective induction of expandable and ontogenetically defined PRRX1+ limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells under defined xeno-free conditions'; cells 'proliferated stably and exhibited the potential to undergo chondrogenic differentiation, formed hyaline cartilaginous-like tissue commensurate to their PRRX1-expression levels'; patient-derived iPSC versions were used to identify therapeutic candidates for type II collagenopathy.

evidence.cite: Takao T, Yamada D & Takarada T 2022, STAR Protoc 3:101786, 'A protocol to induce expandable limb-bud mesenchymal cells from human pluripotent stem cells'
evidence.finding: Step-by-step protocol for selective differentiation of hPSCs into expandable PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchymal (ExpLBM) cells with serial-passage expansion retaining chondrogenic capacity.

evidence.cite: Takao T et al. 2023, Stem Cell Res Ther 14:34, 'A novel chondrocyte sheet fabrication using human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived expandable limb-bud mesenchymal cells'
evidence.finding: ExpLBM-derived chondrocyte sheets were Safranin O, COL2 and ACAN positive, COL1 and RUNX2 negative, and engrafted in osteochondral knee defects in immunodeficient rats.

routes.reversibility: Fully reversible; expandable through serial passage, which is the property that distinguishes it from primary limb-bud mesenchyme.
routes.lethality_risk: None.
routes.specificity: Limb-bud mesenchyme; MESENCHYME ONLY - there is no ectoderm, no AER, no signalling centre. Every AER-dependent route on this page is out of scope for this system.
routes.difficulty: medium; defined, xeno-free and published as a protocol.
routes.what_we_would_run: If a judge asks what we could test tomorrow with no animal, the honest answer is a human mesenchymal readout of a limb genotype. We have no cell-culture arm either, so this too is a proposal - but it is a proposal with a published protocol attached, which is a different kind of claim from a sentence. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: A mesenchyme-only system cannot test the AER-centred half of the design space. Pairing ExpLBM cells with an AER-like population (as budoids do in mouse) has not been published for human that we found.

routes.title: Ex vivo limb-bud organ culture and micromass - manipulate a real bud outside the animal
routes.mechanism: A dissected limb bud can be kept in organ culture, where signalling pathways can be manipulated pharmacologically, gene expression examined and lineages tracked longitudinally. High-density primary limb mesenchymal (micromass) culture models commitment and differentiation of limb progenitors but cannot reproduce assembly into organised tissues spanning the musculoskeletal system. Organ culture keeps the real three-dimensional bud; micromass trades that for throughput.
