routes.intervention: Dissect limb buds at a chosen stage from embryos of a chosen genotype, culture, apply inhibitors or beads, image over time. Tbx4-null hindlimb buds were shown to fail to develop 'either in vivo or in vitro', so the explant reproduces at least some genetic lesions faithfully.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Outgrowth, cartilage condensation and gene expression in a real bud over hours to days. Not a skeleton in an animal, and not a behaviour.

evidence.cite: Arostegui M & Underhill TM 2021, Methods Mol Biol 2230:115-137, 'Murine Limb Bud Organ Cultures for Studying Musculoskeletal Development'
evidence.finding: 'The basic mechanisms regulating the commitment and differentiation of diverse limb progenitor populations has been successfully modeled in vitro using high density primary limb mesenchymal or micromass cultures. However, this approach is limited in its ability to more faithfully recapitulate the assembly of progenitors into organized tissues ... limb bud organ cultures ... have proved to be a powerful model system', with strategies to manipulate signalling pathways, examine gene expression and perform longitudinal lineage tracking. The authors note no organoid system effectively models the complexity of limb development.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2003, Development 130:2681-93
evidence.finding: 'hindlimb buds from Tbx4 mutants fail to develop either in vivo or in vitro' - the explant reproduces the in-vivo genetic failure.

evidence.cite: Czyrek AA et al. 2025, Cell Mol Life Sci 82:167
evidence.finding: Stabilised FGF10 inhibited growth of mouse embryonic TIBIAS in explant and altered limb morphogenesis when implanted into chicken limb buds - an example of the explant/implant readout in current use.

routes.reversibility: Acutely reversible pharmacologically within the culture window.
routes.lethality_risk: Animals are still used to source the buds, so this is a REFINEMENT and a partial reduction, not a replacement. Saying otherwise would overstate it.
routes.specificity: One bud, one stage, one manipulation.
routes.difficulty: low-medium; a standard embryology technique with a published methods chapter.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing today. This matters for the welfare section: it is the route that takes a question out of a born animal and into a dissected embryo, which is the single most effective refinement available for this subject. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Underhill and Arostegui state plainly that no organoid system effectively models limb-development complexity. That was written in 2021; budoids appeared in 2025. The page should present that as a moving front, not a settled verdict.

routes.title: Recombinant limb assay - rebuild a bud from dissociated cells inside a donated ectoderm
routes.mechanism: Undissociated or dissociated-and-reaggregated undifferentiated mesodermal cells are packed into an ectodermal jacket taken from an early limb bud, and the filled ectoderm is grafted onto the back of a host chick embryo. The cells receive nascent embryonic signals and develop complex skeletal elements. This is the only system on this page in which SKELETAL ELEMENTS form from dissociated cells, which is exactly what conventional organoids have not achieved.
routes.intervention: Reaggregate mesenchyme of a chosen genotype or composition, fill a wild-type ectodermal jacket, graft and score skeletal output. The proposal in the source is to use stem cells or other progenitors as the mesodermal input.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Complex skeletal elements - a genuine skeletal readout, in a chimeric graft rather than in a limb position on the animal it came from.

evidence.cite: Garcia-Garcia RD et al. 2022, Front Cell Dev Biol 10:863140, 'Recombinant Limb Assay as in vivo Organoid Model'
evidence.finding: 'Although organoids are widely studied, the formation of skeletal elements in an organoid model has not yet been possible. Therefore, we suggest that the formation of skeletal elements using the recombinant limb (RL) assay system can serve as an in vivo organoid model. RLs are formed from undissociated or dissociated-reaggregated undifferentiated mesodermal cells introduced into an ectodermal cover obtained from an early limb bud ... the cells can receive the nascent embryonic signals and develop complex skeletal elements.'

routes.reversibility: The composition is chosen at assembly; nothing is reversible after grafting.
routes.lethality_risk: Uses chick host embryos and a donor ectoderm, so animals are still involved.
routes.specificity: Skeletal elements from a defined cell mixture - the one system that separates 'which cells' from 'which position in the body'.
routes.difficulty: high; microsurgical, low throughput, and requires chick embryology.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. It is in the design space because it answers a question none of the others can: is limb loss a property of the CELLS or of the SIGNALS they sit in? Putting ZRS-null mesenchyme into a wild-type ectodermal jacket is the experiment that separates those, and as far as our search went it has not been done. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Has anyone run a recombinant limb with mesenchyme from a defined limb-loss genotype? We did not find one; our search was 'limb bud organoid' and 'micromass culture limb bud mesenchyme chondrogenesis screening' on PubMed only.

routes.title: Gastruloids and trunk-like structures - and the limb field that is not in them
routes.mechanism: Mouse ESC aggregates embedded in extracellular matrix self-organise into trunk-like structures with a neural tube frequently flanked by bilateral somites, following the same stepwise gene-regulatory programme as the embryo by single-cell RNA-seq, and reproducing embryonic mutant phenotypes (Tbx6 knockout TLSs develop additional neural tubes). They are the closest thing to an embryo-scale in-vitro system and they establish the trunk axial pattern from which, in an embryo, the lateral plate and limb field arise.
routes.intervention: Would be: extend a TLS protocol to specify lateral plate mesoderm and a limb field, then apply limb-loss lesions in the correct axial context.
routes.predicted_phenotype: NONE YET for limbs. Neither of the TLS papers we read reports a limb field, a limb bud or an AER. This route is on the page as an explicit GAP: the embryo-scale in-vitro system does not currently contain the structure this question is about, and the limb-specific system (budoids) does not contain the trunk.

evidence.cite: Veenvliet JV et al. 2020, Science 370:eaba4937, 'Mouse embryonic stem cells self-organize into trunk-like structures with neural tube and somites'
evidence.finding: mESC aggregates embedded in matrix form 'highly organized trunk-like structures (TLSs) comprising the neural tube and somites'; scRNA-seq confirms the process is 'highly analogous to mouse development and follows the same stepwise gene-regulatory program'; Tbx6 knockout TLSs developed additional neural tubes mirroring the embryonic mutant.

evidence.cite: Bolondi A et al. 2021, Bio Protoc 11:e4042, 'Generation of Mouse Pluripotent Stem Cell-derived Trunk-like Structures'
evidence.finding: Step-by-step protocol: gastruloid morphogenetic potential is unlocked by a low percentage of Matrigel, giving TLSs with a neural tube frequently flanked by bilateral somites, implementable with standard cell culture.

routes.reversibility: Fully; cell culture.
routes.lethality_risk: None.
routes.specificity: Trunk axial structures. No limb.
routes.difficulty: low-medium to make TLSs; unsolved to add a limb field.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. Listing this honestly is the point: the obvious question 'could you just do it in a dish at embryo scale' has the answer 'not yet, because the dish does not make limbs', and the page is stronger for saying so than for implying otherwise. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Has anyone reported lateral plate mesoderm or a limb field in a gastruloid or TLS? Our search on PubMed ('trunk-like structure gastruloid somite organoid mouse embryonic stem cells') returned ONE record and we followed it plus the 2020 Science paper. We did not search bioRxiv, which is where this would appear first. That is the scope of this negative.

recommendation.headline: If the goal is a limbless MOUSE EMBRYO with an unambiguous phenotype: conditional Fgf10 deletion restricted to limb-bud mesenchyme (Prx1-CreER) and induced at a chosen stage. If the goal is a VIABLE ADULT ANIMAL: do not attempt tetra-amelia at all - take one pair, with Tbx5-conditional for forelimb or Tbx4-conditional for hindlimb, or take the ZRS-null, which is the only limb-reduced mouse in this literature with a published photograph of it alive and of normal body size at two weeks.
why: It starts from the strongest phenotype in the literature. Fgf10 loss abolishes AER formation and gives complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs; it is the reference amelia and it is upstream of Fgf8.

It removes the thing that makes that phenotype useless. The germline Fgf10 null dies perinatally from complete absence of lungs - a defect with nothing to do with limbs. Prx1-Cre recombines limb-bud mesenchyme from E9.5 and is never detected in limb-bud ectoderm, so the lung, thyroid, pituitary and salivary gland requirements are outside the domain.

It adds the one axis that the whole field has shown to matter. Naiche and Papaioannou removed Tbx4 at three different times and got three different outcomes, one of which was no phenotype at all. A germline allele cannot express that; an inducible one turns the lesion into an ordered series.
Every component is an existing, published reagent. This is a breeding and dosing programme, not an invention.

It gives a scoreable readout. A skeletal preparation either has an autopod or it does not - which is the property that makes this subject a better benchmark than the open-ended design problems our demo is built on.

honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.preferred: Forelimb-only (Tbx5 conditional) or hindlimb-only (Tbx4 conditional). A mouse missing one pair retains the other and is far more likely to thermoregulate, locomote, groom and reach food than a tetra-amelic animal. Tbx5 is the cleaner of the two in principle because the limb FIELD is correctly patterned in its absence - only the bud is never started - and because the germline Tbx4 null dies at E10.5 from chorioallantoic failure, so Tbx4 work is conditional-only by necessity rather than by choice.
honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.already_demonstrated: The ZRS-null is the one allele in this literature where a limb-reduced mouse has been shown alive: Kvon et al. photographed ZRS-/- animals at two weeks with body size comparable to wild type and truncated limbs. But note what it is - TRUNCATION with a retained stylopod and girdle, not amelia. If the ask is 'a mouse with no limbs that lives', nobody in this literature has published one, and the page should not imply otherwise.
honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.the_trade_off_stated_plainly: Amelia and viability pull against each other at every layer. Every route that reliably abolishes the limb bud (Fgf10, Fgfr2b, Grem1, WNT3, RSPO2, Meis1/2) takes out lung, kidney or the whole WNT system with it, because the genes that start a limb also start other organs. The only two ways out are tissue restriction (Prx1-Cre) and cis-regulation (ZRS, Pitx1 enhancer) - and cis-regulation, the route evolution actually used twice, delivers truncation rather than absence.

what_we_would_run_ourselves: Score the Kvon 2016 ZRS ortholog series with a genome language model, pre-registering the prediction that it separates human and coelacanth (normal limbs) from cobra (none) and places python between them. The coelacanth case is the sharpest test: it shares LESS sequence identity with human ZRS (57%) than python does (59%) and yet behaves like wild type, so identity alone cannot produce the right answer.

Score the 17 bp E1 indel in both directions on both backgrounds. The published result is asymmetric - reintroducing it into python ZRS restores normal limbs, removing it from mouse ZRS does not alter limb-bud expression. A model that returns a symmetric effect has failed a test whose answer is known in advance.
Record the Ushiki human-to-mouse CTCF discordance as an explicit REFUSAL in our cross-scale coupling layer rather than scoring it.

State the dose law in Lean as a law about a model - a monotone map from an activity variable with a threshold band to a distal-element count - and show Lean rejects mutants with the monotonicity flipped and the threshold moved. That proves our reasoning is consistent. It proves nothing about mice, and we would write both sentences together.
what_we_will_not_claim: We have never scored a limb enhancer. Everything above is proposed, not done.

No registered calibration exists anywhere in our system, so no quantitative bridge from a sequence score to a skeletal phenotype is composable today. The strongest honest output is a RANKING over sequences.
A sequence score is not transcription and transcription is not a skeleton.
We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm. A prediction we cannot test is a hypothesis and we would label it as one.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Severe TRUNCATION of both fore- and hindlimbs with a retained stylopod and girdle; viable to at least two weeks with normal body size. Not amelia.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the single best-studied limb enhancer in vertebrates, and Kvon et al. 2016 is the field's strongest precedent for a REGULATORY change, not a knockout, removing limbs from a mouse. If the judge says 'an enhancer' or 'a regulatory element' rather than 'a gene', this is almost certainly it.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there a proximal stump with no autopod (ZRS) or no limb bud at all (Fgf10/WNT3 class)?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: True tetra-amelia - complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs, developing to birth, then perinatally lethal from complete absence of lungs. Also absent thyroid, pituitary and salivary glands.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the canonical limbless mouse and has been since 1998. If the judge's animals had NO limb buds and died at birth, this is the mechanism class.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Did the animals breathe? An Fgf10 null has no lungs.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tetra-amelia - complete absence of all four limbs, with craniofacial and urogenital defects - from a homozygous Q83X nonsense allele in a consanguineous family.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It was the first WNT-gene mutation associated with a Mendelian disorder and it is THE classical human 'gene for limblessness'. Note the authors' own caveat: mouse Wnt3 nulls are early-lethal, so this phenotype exists in humans and not in mice.

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: human (allelic series), Xenopus (reciprocal gain), mouse (Lgr4/5/6 triple KO as a negative)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tetra-amelia syndrome with lung aplasia and total absence of the four limbs; severity graded across an allelic series and correlated with impaired RNF43/ZNRF3 binding. The reciprocal deletion of rnf43 and znrf3 in Xenopus triggers SUPERNUMERARY limbs.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: If the judge's claim is recent and human-genetics-based, this is at least as strong a candidate as WNT3 and arguably stronger: an allelic series, measured biochemistry per allele, and a stated master-switch mechanism. It is also the candidate most likely to be missed, because the older literature points at WNT3.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there lung aplasia alongside the amelia, and was there an allelic series rather than a single family?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Mouse: forelimb buds do not form; hindlimbs normal; the limb field itself is correctly patterned. Human haploinsufficiency gives Holt-Oram syndrome - upper-limb and heart defects, NOT limblessness.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the forelimb initiation gene and it directly activates Fgf10. If the judge's phenotype was forelimb-only, this is the first place to look.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Forelimb only? And was there a cardiac phenotype?

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: mouse, stickleback (PITX1 enhancer), human (small patella syndrome for TBX4; Liebenberg syndrome for PITX1)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tbx4 null: hindlimb field induced and initially patterned, buds fail to develop, embryos die at E10.5 from chorioallantoic failure. Pitx1 null: hindlimb severely impaired but NOT abolished. Pitx1 enhancer deletion in stickleback: viable pelvic loss under positive selection.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: Hindlimb-only phenotype, or work on the stickleback pelvic system. Note Tbx4 does NOT determine hindlimb identity - Pitx1 does.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Hindlimb only? And did the embryos die around E10.5 from the allantois rather than from the limb?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Mouse: 'limbs are absent or truncated' from failure of the AER to differentiate and be maintained, with no stratified skin and absence of all squamous epithelia and their derivatives. Mice are born alive.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the only amelia-class mouse whose lesion is the signalling-centre EPITHELIUM rather than induction or mesenchymal signalling, and it is a prominent human limb-malformation gene. If the judge mentions ectodermal dysplasia alongside the limbs, this is it.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there a skin, hair, tooth or gland phenotype as well?

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: mouse (extra toes, Xt), human (Greig cephalopolysyndactyly, Pallister-Hall)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: POLYDACTYLY with loss of digit identity, not limb loss. And critically, removing Gli3 from a Shh-null background progressively RESTORES distal limb development.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is one of the most-studied limb genes and the one most often confused with a limb-loss gene by people outside the field. Worth naming so the conversation can rule it out quickly and respectfully.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Al-Awadi-Raas-Rothschild syndrome - limb/pelvis/uterus hypoplasia-aplasia. A severe human limb-deficiency condition.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is a genuine human 'limb absence' gene and is in the same WNT family as WNT3 and RSPO2's pathway. We read only a record for which PubMed holds no abstract, so we can confirm the syndrome-gene association and nothing about the phenotype's details beyond the syndrome's own name.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was the pelvis and uterus involved as well as the limbs?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Roberts syndrome - craniofacial anomalies and TETRAPHOCOMELIA (severe shortening, not absence, of all four limbs), with loss of sister-chromatid cohesion at heterochromatic regions.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: Tetraphocomelia is often described colloquially as 'limbless'. It is mechanistically a cohesion/cell-division disorder, not a limb-patterning one, which is a useful and non-obvious distinction to be able to draw.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Were the limbs absent, or were they present and severely shortened?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Limb agenesis when both are inactivated in the lateral plate mesoderm; a three-deleted-allele hypomorph gives proximal hypoplasia and loss of POSTERIOR skeletal elements.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: A recent (2021) agenesis result, upstream of Tbx and co-regulating Fgf10 enhancers. If the judge's work is on limb INITIATION rather than outgrowth, this is current.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was the phenotype dose-dependent across allele number?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Failure to establish a functional AER and the SHH/FGF loop, with the core limb mesenchyme eliminated by apoptosis; neonatal lethal from absent kidneys plus lung septation defects.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the inhibitor arm of the self-terminating loop and a classic limb-bud gene. Also implicated comparatively: a rapidly evolving GREM1 conserved non-coding element in marine mammals.

welfare.framing: A limbless mouse is a severe phenotype. This section is here because a reviewer will expect it and because its absence would be a hole in the page, not as an apology for the science. The relevant question for a licence or IACUC review is not whether the phenotype is severe - it is - but whether the severity is necessary for the question, and whether a less severe route answers it.

severity_classification.point: European severity classification under Directive 2010/63/EU applies to the BREEDING AND MAINTENANCE of genetically altered lines likely to develop a harmful phenotype, not only to experimental procedures. A line that is limbless at birth is authorised as a harmful-phenotype line before any experiment is performed.
severity_classification.evidence_cite: Zintzsch A et al. 2017, Lab Anim 51:573-582, 'Guidelines on severity assessment and classification of genetically altered mouse and rat lines'
severity_classification.evidence_finding: 'Genetic alterations can unpredictably compromise the wellbeing of animals ... the breeding and maintenance of genetically altered (GA) animals which are likely to develop a harmful phenotype has to be authorized.' The Working Group of Berlin Animal Welfare Officers provides a list of symptoms classified as non-harmful, mild, moderate or severe, with monitoring and refinement strategies and specific housing requirements.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Do not let the animal be born. Analyse at E18.5 by skeletal preparation, at E11.5 by reporter assay, at E10.5 by in-situ hybridisation - which is precisely the protocol Kvon et al. used for everything except the two-week viability photograph. The entire ZRS allelic series was characterised on embryos.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: You learn nothing about postnatal viability, locomotion, growth or welfare - which is exactly the question a 'can you make a limbless mouse' claim turns on.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Use a tissue-restricted conditional (Prx1-Cre) so the lesion does not also remove lungs or kidneys. This both improves the science and removes a large, certain source of suffering that is not even the phenotype of interest.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Breeding complexity; a craniofacial domain in the driver that must be checked.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Use an inducible allele so the lesion is applied in the window that matters. A gene removed after its requirement has passed gives no phenotype at all - Naiche and Papaioannou showed this directly for Tbx4 - so stage selection is a way of asking a sharper question with fewer affected animals.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Tamoxifen effects on pregnancy require vehicle controls.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Take one pair rather than four. A forelimb-only or hindlimb-only animal retains locomotion and is a materially less severe phenotype than tetra-amelia, and for most mechanistic questions it answers the same thing.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: None scientifically, for questions about one limb's network.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Replace with ex vivo limb-bud organ culture, where signalling can be manipulated pharmacologically and lineages tracked longitudinally. Tbx4-null hindlimb buds fail to develop in vitro as they do in vivo, so explants reproduce at least some genetic lesions faithfully.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Animals are still used to source the buds, so this is a refinement and a partial reduction, NOT a replacement, and calling it a replacement would overstate it.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Replace with budoids - mESC-derived organoids containing AER-like, surface-ectoderm and limb-mesoderm cells, undergoing chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking, at >1,000 budoids per differentiation - or with human iPSC-derived PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchyme. These are true replacements and they are scalable.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: The readouts are cell fate, polarisation and cartilage, not a skeleton and not an animal. No dish currently makes a limb; the Underhill/Arostegui methods chapter said in 2021 that no organoid system effectively modelled limb-development complexity, and budoids (2025) are a real advance on that but not a refutation of it.

what_a_licence_or_iacuc_review_would_tur: Is the severe phenotype necessary for the question, or would a one-pair, conditional, or embryonic-only version answer it? For most mechanistic questions the answer is that it would.
Is a non-animal route available for this specific readout? For cell-fate and signalling questions in 2026, increasingly yes; for skeletal and postnatal questions, no.
What is the humane endpoint and who decides it? A limbless neonate cannot right itself, reach a nipple or thermoregulate normally.
What are the housing requirements? The Berlin guidelines pair severity classification with specific housing and monitoring requirements rather than treating classification as a paperwork exercise.

How many animals does the breeding scheme produce for each informative one? A homozygous conditional on two floxed alleles plus a driver is a demanding cross, and reduction is a breeding-design problem as much as an experimental one.

Precedent exists and is documented: the Kvon et al. transgenic and knock-in work was reviewed and approved by the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Animal Welfare and Research Committee, mice were monitored daily and inspected weekly by the committee chair, the head of the facility and veterinary staff, and the facility is AAALAC-accredited. Embryonic samples for in-situ and skeletal preparation were dissected blind to genotype, and knock-in and knock-out experiments used a matched-littermate design.
welfare.our_position: We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm. Nothing on this page was performed by us and no organism, embryo or cell was made by us. The welfare discussion is here because the design space we are describing is one somebody else would have to execute, and a design space presented without its costs is not a design space.

limitations: We ran no experiments. Every route on this page is a reading of someone else's published work, or an explicitly labelled proposal. Nothing here is a result of ours.

ONE source was read at full text (Kvon et al. 2016, via PMC5484524, including figure legends and STAR Methods). Everything else is read at ABSTRACT level, with one exception noted below. No claim on this page is written in the voice of having read a body we did not read.

Summerbell 1974 (PMID 4463222) is cited at LISTING level: the PubMed record resolves and its title and MeSH terms confirm a quantitative AER-excision series in chick, but PubMed holds no abstract for it, so we have read no result statement from that paper and make no quantitative claim from it. The classical premise is restated independently by Lewandoski et al. 2000.

Garavelli et al. 2010 (PMID 21271649, WNT7A / Al-Awadi-Raas-Rothschild) also has no abstract in PubMed. We confirm the syndrome-gene association from the title and MeSH terms and state nothing further about the phenotype.
Every PMID on this page was retrieved from PubMed and resolved to a record during this session; none is quoted from memory or from a secondary summary. DOIs are as returned by PubMed.

SCOPE OF NEGATIVE SEARCHES. All searches were PubMed only, in English, via the pubmed MCP tools. We did not search bioRxiv, medRxiv, patents, theses or non-English sources, and PubMed's query parser ANDs all terms, so a long query returns fewer results than a short one - several of our early searches returned zero for that reason and were repeated with shorter terms. Specific negatives: (1) no molecular mechanism for Lerista limb reduction was found ('Lerista limb reduction skink evolution' returned 4 records, all taxonomic, morphometric or macroevolutionary); (2) no published genetic AER ablation with diphtheria toxin was found ('diphtheria toxin ablation apical ectodermal ridge genetic mouse' returned 4 records, none of them an AER ablation); (3) no auxin-inducible degron study in mouse embryos was found, so the degron route cites dTAG/FKBP work instead; (4) no limb field was found reported in gastruloids or trunk-like structures, searched on PubMed only, which is the wrong place to look first for a 2026 result; (5) no published Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox limb series was found, which is why our own recommendation is labelled 'proposed'; (6) no recombinant-limb experiment using mesenchyme from a defined limb-loss genotype was found. Each of these is an absence in OUR search, not an absence in the literature.

Phenotype statements are quoted or closely paraphrased from the abstracts. Where a paper's own authors flag an inference rather than a measurement - Thewissen et al. on HAND2 association, Sun et al. on cetacean ZRS activity, the 41 Ma and 34 Ma dates - we mark it as theirs and do not restate it as a measurement.

The two published human-to-mouse discordances on this page (Ushiki on CTCF/acheiropodia; Niemann on WNT3 viability) are a standing warning that cross-species transfer of a cis-regulatory or viability claim is unsafe, and we did not systematically check every other route for the same risk.

Two founding Fgf10 papers DISAGREE about whether the limb bud initiates: Min et al. 1998 say initiation was abolished, Sekine et al. 1999 say bud formation initiated but outgrowth did not occur. We preserve the disagreement rather than reconciling it.
Route counts are not evidence counts. 'evidence_strength: proposed' appears on four routes and means exactly what it says: nobody has done it. A design space is not a list of results.

We have never scored a limb enhancer, have no registered calibration anywhere in our system, and have performed no functional validation of any sequence-model output we have produced. Any claim about predicting limb phenotype from sequence is a hypothesis and is labelled as one.
routes.attribution: Bibliographic records and abstracts cited here were retrieved from PubMed (NCBI) on 2026-11-01; the DOI of every cited article is given in `sources`. Kvon et al. 2016 was additionally retrieved in full text from PubMed Central (PMC5484524).

studies.title: The ZRS across species: what changes when a limb enhancer is swapped
studies.question: Kvon et al. swapped the mouse ZRS for orthologs from other species: human and coelacanth gave normal limbs, python and king cobra truncated them. The python ZRS is about as similar to mouse as the coelacanth's is, so whatever separates them is not overall sequence similarity. What can you see in the alignment, and what can't you?
studies.summary: Real ZRS orthologs fetched from NCBI, aligned here, with per-column conservation and ETS1 motif positions. The contrast of interest is between the orthologs that gave normal limbs in the published knock-in and the ones that truncated them. This is a correlational reading of a handful of sequences; it is not a predictor of enhancer activity and is not used as one anywhere on this page. The causal evidence is Kvon et al.'s mouse genetics, not this alignment.
studies.code: results/limbless-mouse/code/final_analysis.py (with fetch_orthologs.py, locate_zrs.py, core_trim.py, make_figure.py and zrs_lib.py beside it)

data.method:
Goal: a comparative, sequence-level picture of the ZRS limb enhancer across species whose orthologs Kvon et al. (2016) swapped into the mouse, to see what distinguishes the orthologs that supported normal limbs from the one that truncated them.

1. REFERENCE. The mouse ZRS was taken as the exact 1,324 bp interval Kvon et al. deleted by CRISPR, mm10 chr5:29,314,497-29,315,820 (their Figure S3), fetched from GRCm38.p6 NC_000071.6. Positive control that this is the right interval: the fetched sequence is exactly 1,324 bp and contains the paper's stated sgRNA recognition sequence (AGTACCATGCGTGTGTGTGA) on the minus strand at offset 16, i.e. 'in close proximity to its 5-prime border' as the paper describes; a 1-nt mutated copy of that motif is absent.

2. ORTHOLOG RETRIEVAL. Kvon et al. deposited NO GenBank accessions for the ZRS orthologs - the sequences are in supplementary Tables S2/S3 and the constructs were chemically synthesised - and those supplementary PDFs could not be retrieved (see limitations). Orthologs were therefore re-derived from public genomes: for each species the annotated LMBR1 locus (the ZRS lies in LMBR1 intron 5) was fetched with a 10 kb flank, and the ZRS was located inside it by unique 12-mer seeding from the mouse ZRS followed by local affine-gap alignment (Biopython PairwiseAligner). Where a snake had diverged so far from mouse that only a short block aligned, the Burmese python ZRS - itself mouse-anchored - was used as a bridging anchor; the anchor used is recorded per species. Human was taken from GRCh38 chromosome 7 and cross-checked against the dedicated RefSeq record NG_042169.2 ('Homo sapiens ZPA regulatory sequence (ZRS)'), which matches the fetched window exactly while a 1-nt mutant of it does not. King cobra came from scaffold183.1 of assembly AZIM01, the same king cobra assembly Kvon et al. used.

3. ALIGNMENT. All detected orthologs were aligned with MAFFT v7.525 L-INS-i, the same program and mode the paper used. The fetched 1.3 kb windows extend beyond the conserved enhancer, and in those flanks the sequences are not homologous at nucleotide resolution; MAFFT fills them with arbitrary gaps, which manufactures 'shared deletions' that are artefacts. (This was caught by eye: the non-snake blocks aligned there share no similarity with each other.) So, as Kvon et al. did with Gblocks, the alignment was trimmed to its alignable core and realigned: mouse positions were scored by column depth and conservation, smoothed over 31 positions, and the longest run with conservation >= 0.70 and depth >= 0.80 was kept. That core is mouse ZRS 398-1043 (646 bp), mm10 chr5:29,314,894-29,315,539. Every quantitative result below is computed on the realigned core.

4. MOTIFS. Each species' core was scanned on both strands with the JASPAR ETS1 matrix MA0098.3 (consensus ACCGGAAGTG), using a log-odds threshold derived by exact convolution of the score distribution under a uniform background so that p < 0.0032 means what it means in FIMO - the threshold Kvon et al. state. Controls: the consensus scores 15.94 bits and passes; poly-G, poly-C and poly-A all fail.

5. HUMAN DISEASE VARIANTS. All 694 ClinVar LMBR1 variants were fetched and filtered to those falling inside the human ZRS record's GRCh38 interval, then mapped through the alignment by coordinate arithmetic. No variant position was taken from memory or from prose.

limitations: This is a correlational, post-hoc analysis of a handful of sequences. It is NOT a predictor. With two knock-in species that gave normal limbs and two that truncated, no statistic computed here has the power to establish that any sequence feature causes the phenotype; the causal evidence is Kvon et al.'s mouse knock-ins, not this alignment.

The sequences analysed are NOT the sequences Kvon et al. knocked in. Theirs were synthesised from supplementary Tables S2/S3, which could not be retrieved. These were re-derived from reference genomes, so they may differ from the constructs by assembly errors, strain or individual polymorphism, and by window boundaries.

Species substitutions were necessary and change what the comparison means: the paper used boa constrictor (Assemblathon 2 assembly, not in NCBI) and speckled rattlesnake Crotalus mitchellii (JPMF01); this analysis uses Eryx miliaris (dwarf sand boa, a different basal snake, from a dedicated GenBank ZRS record) and Crotalus tigris. Thamnophis elegans was added and is not in the paper at all. Viper (JTGP01) was not analysed.

Percent identity depends heavily on how much flanking sequence is included, and there is no single correct number. Mouse-human is 88.3% over the trimmed core, 78.6% over the full 1.3 kb window, and 85-86% over the best-aligning block alone. Kvon et al. state 73% for human vs mouse; they do not define the metric, so these numbers are NOT directly comparable to theirs and the discrepancy is a definitional difference, not a contradiction of either result.

The core boundaries (mouse 398-1043) come from thresholds on a smoothed conservation profile. The thresholds were chosen by reading the profile's shoulder, but they are choices, and the identity numbers shift if they move.

ETS site numbering E0-E4 from Kvon et al. is NOT reproduced. Their site coordinates were in inaccessible supplementary material, so no site here is claimed to be 'the' E1, E2 etc. Every motif call is marked inferred. The one exception in strength of evidence is the 17 bp deletion block, which was located independently by alignment and which the paper also describes as overlapping an ETS site.
A PWM hit is a sequence match, not a measurement of binding. No ChIP, EMSA or reporter data were used here, and FIMO itself was not run - an equivalent threshold was recomputed.

The corn snake negative ('no ZRS detected') is scoped: the whole annotated LMBR1 locus plus 10 kb either side was searched with 12-mer seeding and local alignment using BOTH the mouse and the Burmese python ZRS as queries. It does not exclude a ZRS remnant elsewhere in the corn snake genome, nor one too diverged for these queries to find.

Rattlesnake could not be assessed at the 17 bp site: MAFFT places unrelated sequence in those columns rather than a gap, so it is reported as not assessable there rather than as retaining the site. Its ETS1 scan returns no hit in that block.
Alignment of sequences this diverged is itself uncertain. Different aligners or parameters will move indel placement, and the snake columns are where that uncertainty is largest.
Model fidelity is not biological validity: reproducing Kvon et al.'s observations says these sequence relationships are real, not that any interpretation of limb loss built on them is.

studies.title: The SHH–GREM1–FGF loop: where a weakened enhancer stops being a weaker limb and starts being no limb
studies.question: The limb bud is held open by a feedback loop. If a ZRS allele lowers ZPA Shh output, is the result proportionally smaller, or is there a threshold below which the loop never engages at all?
studies.summary: An ODE model of the SHH–GREM1–BMP–FGF feedback loop, built from the published topology with every rate constant marked sourced or assumed. The wild-type control must initiate, sustain and self-terminate before any sweep is read. Three knobs are then swept — ZPA Shh output, AER-inducing FGF10 input, and GREM1 production — because three different routes on this page act on three different parts of the same loop. The result that bears hardest on the question: in this model the ZRS knob is near-digital rather than a graded dial. Limbs stay normal down to about half of wild-type ZPA Shh output, the truncated band is narrow (s between 0.32 and 0.48, 17 of 201 settings swept), and below 0.31 the loop never engages at all. If that holds in an embryo, a designed ZRS allelic series would not give a smooth phenotypic series — but it is a property of this model's excitable topology, and nothing here establishes that it holds in an embryo.

variables.units: fraction of Grem1-competent mesenchyme displaced, in [0,1]

edges.claim: AER FGF4 signalling maintains the polarizing region (SHH/FGF4 feedback loop).
SHH signalling is required for maintenance of Gremlin.
BMP4 first initiates Grem1; SHH then propagates it (differential transcriptional regulation of Grem1).
The secreted BMP antagonist Gremlin relays the SHH signal by antagonising BMP.
Gremlin-mediated BMP antagonism is what induces Fgf4 in the AER; BMP therefore represses AER Fgf and GREM1 de-represses it.
FGF signalling can repress Grem1 expression (a novel Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop); the repression is dependent on high FGF activity.
Shh-expressing cells and their descendants cannot express Gremlin; their proliferation forms a barrier separating the Shh signal from Gremlin-expressing cells, which breaks down the Shh-Fgf4 loop.
The expanding former-ZPA descendant zone is refractory to Grem1 expression, so it removes Grem1-competent mesenchyme.
Readout edge. In Fgf10-null mice limb bud formation initiates but outgrowth does not occur and the AER does not form, so AER FGF is taken as the proximate driver of progenitor expansion.

parameters.name: d_S

parameters.note: Not a free parameter; it sets the clock.

parameters.name: K_FS
parameters.note: AER FGF level at which ZPA Shh maintenance is half-maximal. No measured dose-response for AER-FGF -> Shh exists; set below the operating FGF level so the wild-type loop is maintained, not marginal.

parameters.name: d_B

model.nondimensionalisation: Time is measured in SHH turnover times (d_S = 1 by definition). Each species is scaled by its own maximum, so the unantagonised BMP steady state and the underepressed AER FGF steady state are both 1.0 at wild-type settings. This removes 2 parameters (d_S is fixed to 1 by the time unit; b_prod is fixed by d_B so that maximal BMP is 1) and makes every Hill constant readable as a fraction of maximum. 21 of the 23 parameters remain free, and all 21 are labelled assumed; none is labelled sourced.

Removing the Verheyden & Sun 2008 FGF-|Grem1 repression instead leaves termination intact and lengthens the window by +4.0%. The two published mechanisms are therefore NOT equal partners here, and the model leans almost entirely on one of them.

phenotype_classes.no-limb: The loop never engages (AER FGF never exceeds F_on = 0.35) and accumulated outgrowth is below 5% of the wild-type control. In the model this means 'this feedback loop contributed no outgrowth'. It does NOT mean amelia in an embryo: the model contains no SHH-independent proximal outgrowth, so it cannot distinguish a Shh-null limb (which in mice still forms a stylopod) from true limb absence.
phenotype_classes.truncated: The loop engages and self-terminates, but accumulated outgrowth is between 5% and 85% of the wild-type control.
phenotype_classes.normal: The loop engages, self-terminates, and accumulated outgrowth is within 85%-115% of the wild-type control.
phenotype_classes.overgrowth: The loop engages and self-terminates, but accumulated outgrowth exceeds 115% of the wild-type control.
phenotype_classes.fails-to-terminate: AER FGF is still above F_on at the end of the simulated window (t = 80 SHH turnover times). The loop has no off switch in this parameter regime.

limitations: This is a SIMULATION. No quantity in this file is an observation of any embryo.

The model is a caricature of a signalling TOPOLOGY. It is not calibrated to any measured mouse limb bud: no concentration, rate, diffusion length or developmental time in it was fitted to data, and none should be read as one.

21 of the 23 parameters are assumed and none is sourced; the other 2 are fixed by the non-dimensionalisation. They were chosen so the wild-type arm initiates, is maintained and self-terminates -- that is, the control arm's qualitative behaviour was an input to parameter choice, not an independent result.
A threshold in this model is a threshold in this model. It is not a prediction of the ZRS allelic series at which a mouse loses a limb, and it has no units that could be compared to one.

The model is non-spatial: SHH, GREM1, BMP and FGF are single well-mixed levels. The real loop is spatially organised across an epithelial-mesenchymal boundary with measured gradients, and the Scherz 2004 mechanism it borrows is explicitly geometric (an expanding descendant zone). Variable Z is a zero-dimensional stand-in for that geometry.

The model contains no SHH-independent proximal outgrowth, so it cannot distinguish a Shh-null limb -- which in mice still forms proximal skeleton -- from true amelia. Its 'no-limb' class means only 'this loop never engaged'.

Digit number and digit pattern are outside the model. Sheth et al. 2012 (PMID 23239739) show digit patterning is a Turing-type mechanism whose wavelength distal Hox genes set; none of that is represented here, so the model says nothing about how many digits form.
The knob s is held constant in time. In python hindlimb buds the reported defect is that SHH is weak AND transient (PMID 27773569); a time-varying s is not explored.
Only the classifier's boundaries, not the model, decide where 'truncated' ends and 'normal' begins. Those cuts (5%, 85%, 115% of the wild-type control) are assumed.
The outgrowth window duration is most sensitive to k_Z, a wholly assumed parameter. No sensitivity analysis over the full parameter space was run.

The two published termination mechanisms are not equal partners in this parameterisation. The ablation arm shows the loop leans almost entirely on the Scherz 2004 descendant-zone ratchet: without it the loop never terminates, while without the Verheyden & Sun 2008 FGF-|Grem1 repression it still terminates, about 4% later. So the self-terminating behaviour shown in the control figure is mostly one mechanism, and which mechanism dominates in a real limb bud is not addressed here.

studies.title: Skeletal elements as a Turing pattern: how small a limb bud can be and still make a digit
studies.question: If a truncated bud is a smaller field, how small does the field have to get before it patterns no complete skeletal element at all?
studies.summary: A two-dimensional BMP–SOX9–WNT reaction–diffusion model on a limb-bud-shaped domain with a proximodistal FGF gradient, with its own linear-stability analysis as an internal control. Element counts come from a pre-declared objective criterion, not from looking at the pictures, and the spread across random seeds is reported because Turing patterns are seed-dependent. The strongest result is a unification: in this model every route to zero skeletal elements is the same geometric condition — the Turing-permissive region has to be at least about one wavelength across. Shrinking the bud shrinks that region in space; de-tuning the network shrinks it in parameter space, and the FGF gradient maps parameter space onto the proximodistal axis, so it shrinks in space too. Eleven of its 20 parameters are sourced, and they are sourced from a catshark fin rather than a mouse.
studies.code: results/limbless-mouse/code/digit_turing.py (--figures redraws from digit-turing-results-cache.json without re-running the 179 simulations)

data.what_this_is: A SIMULATION of skeletal-element patterning by a Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing network in a limb-bud-shaped domain. No value in this file is an observation, a measurement, or a reproduction of published data. The element counts, wavelengths and critical domain size are properties of this model at these parameters and nothing else.

model.name: BSW (Bmp-Sox9-Wnt) Turing network with a proximodistal Fgf gradient

variables.note: D_S = 0; Sox9 is cell-autonomous (sourced: onimaru2016 states the system has one non-diffusive molecule, Sox9).
static normalised gradient from the distal margin (the AER)

equations_latex.Sox9: \frac{\partial S}{\partial t} = \beta\left(k_2 B - k_3 W - S^3\right)
equations_latex.Bmp: \frac{\partial B}{\partial t} = \beta\left(\alpha_B - (1-k_F F)\,k_4 S - k_5 B + D_B \nabla^2 B\right)
equations_latex.Wnt: \frac{\partial W}{\partial t} = \beta\left(\alpha_W - k_7 k_F F\,S - k_9 W + D_W \nabla^2 W\right)
equations_latex.Fgf: F(\hat{x}) = F_{\max}\,e^{-g\,\hat{x}},\qquad \hat{x} = \frac{\text{distance proximal from the distal margin}}{L_{PD}}

topology.evidence: onimaru2016 eq (16), full-text; cubic self-damping, the only nonlinearity
onimaru2016 Results, 'repressing k4 and boosting k7', full-text
onimaru2016 Results, 'repressing k4 and boosting k7', full-text

parameters.name: beta
parameters.source: onimaru2016 Methods, 'Parameter values were beta=8, ...' for Figs 4-5
parameters.note: Global coefficient controlling the speed of pattern appearance.

parameters.name: k2
parameters.note: Bmp -> Sox9 activation strength. Onimaru et al. perturb exactly this parameter to represent Bmp inhibition.

parameters.name: k3
parameters.note: Wnt -| Sox9 inhibition strength (the minus sign is explicit in eq 16).

parameters.name: k4
parameters.note: Sox9 -| Bmp inhibition strength; repressed by Fgf.

parameters.name: k7
parameters.note: Sox9 -| Wnt inhibition strength; boosted by Fgf.

parameters.name: k5
parameters.note: Bmp linear decay.

parameters.name: k9
parameters.note: Wnt linear decay.

parameters.name: kF
parameters.note: Strength with which the normalised Fgf field F in [0,1] modulates k4 and k7.

parameters.name: D_B
parameters.note: Bmp diffusion. Bmp is the LONG-range species (D_B > D_W).

parameters.name: D_W
parameters.note: Wnt diffusion. Wnt is the SHORT-range species.

parameters.name: alpha_B
parameters.note: Constant Bmp production.

parameters.name: alpha_W
parameters.source: CHANGED from the published value alpha_W = 1.2 (onimaru2016 Methods).
parameters.note: alpha_W = k2*alpha_B*k9/(k3*k5) = 0.03333, chosen so the homogeneous steady state sits exactly at S*=0, where the cubic self-damping -3S*^2 vanishes and the paper's own LINEAR Turing conditions apply. With the published alpha_W = 1.2 my own linear stability analysis finds NO Turing instability anywhere on this static domain: see linear_stability.published_set_check in the JSON. This is the single substantive departure from the published parameter set and it is the reason the whole set must be read as 'published form, operating point retuned'.

parameters.name: F_max
parameters.source: no published value for this geometry
parameters.note: Distal maximum of the normalised Fgf field. Chosen just BELOW the upper edge of the Turing window in F (F_hopf, computed by the LSA below), so that no part of the bud sits in the uniform (q=0) instability regime. Calibration choice.

parameters.name: F_decay
parameters.source: onimaru2016 gives exp(-3*x) on a UNIT SQUARE (Supplementary Fig. 7); the fin/limb simulations instead solve a reaction-diffusion Fgf field whose absolute spatial scale is set by their mesh, which I do not have.
parameters.note: F(x_hat) = F_max * exp(-F_decay * x_hat), x_hat = normalised distance proximal from the distal margin. F_decay=4 (vs the published square-domain 3) makes the Turing-permissive band about one wavelength deep, which is what yields a single proximodistal row of elements rather than two rows.

parameters.name: L_PD
parameters.note: Proximodistal length of the paddle.

parameters.name: W_AP_half
parameters.note: Half-width of the paddle at its distal margin. L_PD and W_AP_half were chosen so that the WILD-TYPE-LIKE run yields about five elements. The five-element outcome is therefore IMPOSED by the domain, not predicted. What the model predicts is how the element count MOVES when the wavelength or the domain is changed.

parameters.name: dx
parameters.note: Grid spacing; checked by the grid-refinement arm.

parameters.name: dt
parameters.source: numerical choice (onimaru2016 use dt=0.002 with an explicit Heun solver; this script uses a semi-implicit solver, so a larger step is admissible)
parameters.note: Checked by the dt-refinement arm. dt=0.02 was measured to be numerically UNSTABLE here; dt=0.01, 0.005 and 0.002 agree to 5 significant figures.

parameters.name: T_end
parameters.note: The pattern coarsens after onset and the coarsening ARRESTS by t~40 (measured in a 1-D control out to t=320). T_end=60 is past arrest.

parameters.name: noise_amplitude
parameters.source: onimaru2016 use 1% Gaussian MULTIPLICATIVE noise at each step; multiplicative noise vanishes identically at this model's steady state S*=0, so it cannot be used here.
parameters.note: Seeded additive Gaussian perturbation of S at t=0, s.d. 1% of the Bmp steady state. A control arm adds dt-scaled per-step additive noise instead.

parameter_provenance_summary.statement: The EQUATION FORM and 11 of 19 parameters are sourced at full-text level from onimaru2016, which states that it implements the raspopovic2014 mouse BSW model. One sourced parameter (alpha_W) was CHANGED, for the reason recorded in its entry and measured in linear_stability.published_set_check. The geometry, the Fgf gradient shape, and all numerical parameters are assumed. The mouse parameter set of raspopovic2014 could not be obtained: that paper is subscription-only and was read at abstract level.

linear_stability.method: Eigenvalues of the 3x3 Jacobian M(q) of the full nonlinear system, linearised about the homogeneous steady state, with the diffusion terms -D_B q^2 and -D_W q^2 on the diagonal and D_S = 0, evaluated on a grid of 6001 wavenumbers q in [0, 1.2]. Turing instability is declared when max Re sigma(0) < 0 AND max_q Re sigma(q) > 0 at q > 0. The homogeneous steady states are the real roots of the cubic in S obtained by eliminating B and W.

turing_window_in_F.note: below F_low the uniform state is stable (no pattern); above F_high it is unstable at q=0 (uniform runaway, not a Turing pattern). F_max was set to 0.62, just below F_high.

published_set_check.question: Is the published parameter set, with alpha_W = 1.2, Turing-unstable on this static domain?
published_set_check.scope: 51 values of F in [0,1]; every real homogeneous steady state at each (1 to 3 roots); 6001 wavenumbers in [0,1.2].
published_set_check.diagnosis: With alpha_W = 1.2 the homogeneous steady state lies far from S = 0 (S* between about -5.8 and -0.58 on the branch that is continuous in F), so the cubic self-damping term -3S*^2 is large and suppresses the instability. The one state with a positive growth rate is unstable already at q = 0, which is a uniform instability, not a Turing instability.
published_set_check.what_this_does_and_does_not_mean: This is NOT a claim that the published model is wrong. onimaru2016 run it on a GROWING catshark fin mesh with per-step noise and a reaction-diffusion Fgf field whose absolute spatial scale is set by a mesh I do not have, and their published Turing-space analysis uses the LINEAR model (k1 = 0, so f_S = 0) with k3 = 1, not the cubic model with k3 = 3. My test is a static homogeneous domain and is not like-for-like. What it does mean is that I could not reproduce a Turing instability from the published numbers as I read them, so the operating point here is mine and is labelled assumed.

measured_wavelength.two_d_measurement: mean spacing between the anteroposterior centroids of adjacent counted elements, averaged over the 6 wild-type seeds. This is the pattern's own wavelength and it is the one used for the critical domain size.
measured_wavelength.one_d_uniform_control_note: 1-D periodic domain of length 1500 at a uniform Fgf level, spectral diffusion, probed at t=2 (still linear) and at t=160 (saturated). The three F values span the Turing-permissive band of the 2-D paddle.

comparison_to_linear_prediction.verdict: THEY DISAGREE, by a factor of about two, and the disagreement is reported rather than tuned away. The linear analysis predicts the FASTEST-GROWING mode at onset; the simulated pattern then coarsens and the coarsening arrests at a longer, nonlinearly selected wavelength. The agreement that does hold is in the LINEAR regime: a 1-D uniform-domain run probed at t = 2, while the amplitude is still small, has a dominant wavelength close to the LSA value (45 against 43 at F=0.62). Coarsening was measured to arrest by t ~ 40 and the wavelength was then unchanged out to t = 320. The 2-D measured spacing is shorter than the 1-D saturated wavelength at F = 0.62 because the 2-D permissive band spans a range of F, not just its distal maximum, and is only about one wavelength deep.

sweep_descriptions.diffusion_scale: D_B and D_W scaled together by this factor. lambda scales as sqrt(factor). This is the WAVELENGTH KNOB. Direction check: shorter wavelength should give MORE, thinner elements, which is the direction sheth2012 reports for progressive loss of distal Hox dose (read at abstract level; no number taken from it).
sweep_descriptions.fgf_strength_kF: Strength of the Fgf modulation of k4 and k7. Moves the system through the Turing window and changes where the permissive band sits.
sweep_descriptions.domain_scale: Linear scale factor on the whole paddle, Fgf gradient scaling with it. This is the bridge to a truncated limb bud.
sweep_descriptions.bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced: THIS IS THE CRITICALITY KNOB. k2 and alpha_W are scaled by the same factor, which changes the Bmp->Sox9 coupling strength while leaving the operating point exactly at S* = 0 (the balance k2*alpha_B/k5 = k3*alpha_W/k9 is preserved under a common factor, and S* = 0 was verified at every value). The linear-stability growth rate falls monotonically from factor 0.85 upwards and the Turing instability is LOST at factor 5.5 (max Re sigma over all q and all F in the bud becomes negative). Above that the field stays at the homogeneous steady state: a uniform Sox9 field and no skeletal elements, with no change to the domain and no change to the wavelength mechanism.
sweep_descriptions.bmp_to_sox9_k2_alone: Strength of Bmp activation of Sox9, varied ON ITS OWN. onimaru2016 perturb exactly this parameter to represent Bmp inhibition. READ THIS ONE WITH CARE and prefer bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced: in this retuned model the homogeneous steady state sits at S* = 0 only when k2*alpha_B/k5 = k3*alpha_W/k9, which with the other values here means only at k2 = 1. Changing k2 alone therefore moves the operating point as well as the coupling, and the two effects cannot be separated. That is why every value except 1 collapses to a single fused domain. The sweep is kept because that fragility is a real property of the assumed operating point and hiding it would misrepresent the model.
sweep_descriptions.wnt_production_alphaW_scale: Multiplier on alpha_W, the constant Wnt production term. READ THIS ONE WITH CARE. onimaru2016 perturb Wnt production and report partial fusion of Sox9 into continuous domains, matched in vivo by a porcupine inhibitor, and that is what the fused class here looks like. BUT in this retuned model alpha_W also sets the operating point: S* = 0 only at the one value alpha_W = k2*alpha_B*k9/(k3*k5), and moving alpha_W moves S* away from zero, which switches the cubic self-damping -3S*^2 back on. So this sweep measures the FRAGILITY OF THE ASSUMED OPERATING POINT at least as much as it measures a Wnt perturbation, and the two cannot be separated in this parameterisation. It is reported because that fragility is a real and unflattering property of the choice made here, not because it is a clean perturbation.

one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.statement: In this model every route to zero skeletal elements is the same geometric condition: the Turing-PERMISSIVE REGION must be at least about one wavelength across. Shrinking the bud shrinks that region in space; de-tuning the network shrinks it in parameter space, and therefore also in space, because the Fgf gradient maps parameter space onto the proximodistal axis.
one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.evidence_from_the_domain_sweep: Elements disappear below about 0.9 wavelengths of anteroposterior width.
one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.evidence_from_the_coupling_sweep: At Bmp-Sox9 coupling x5 the linear analysis still reports a Turing instability (max growth +0.31 per time unit), but the simulation forms nothing. The reason is geometric and is computable from the LSA: at that coupling the Turing window has narrowed to F in (0.596, 1.0), and with F_max = 0.62 and F = F_max*exp(-4*x_hat) over L_PD = 300, the permissive strip is only about 3.0 model length units deep, against a wavelength of 18.6 there - under a fifth of a wavelength, and narrower than one grid cell. At coupling x4 the strip is about 13.7 units against a wavelength of 24.9, roughly 0.55 wavelengths, and the counts are correspondingly marginal and seed-dependent (1, 3, 1).
one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.consequence: The simulated loss of pattern (coupling x5) comes BEFORE the formal loss of linear instability (x5.5). Both numbers are reported; the simulated one is the one that would be observable.

critical_domain_size.axis: anteroposterior width of the paddle at its widest point
critical_domain_size.definition: Midpoint between the largest domain scale with a mean element count of exactly zero and the smallest with a non-zero mean, expressed in units of the measured wavelength lambda_meas. The uncertainty is half that interval and is set by the spacing of the domain_scale grid, not by a fit.
critical_domain_size.rule_sensitivity: THE CRITICAL SIZE DEPENDS ON THE COUNTING RULE, by about a factor of two, and both numbers are given. The revised rule requires a surviving component to be at least 0.10 * lambda_meas^2; the original required only 0.10 * lambda_lin^2, which is about four times smaller in area and so still counts a partial condensation in a bud too small to hold a whole one. Quote the range, not one end of it.
critical_domain_size.reading: Somewhere between about half a wavelength and about one and a quarter wavelengths of anteroposterior width, the paddle stops being able to hold an element and the field is unpatterned. Because the Fgf gradient scales with the bud, the proximodistal permissive band shrinks at the same time, so both axes run out together; the AP figure is the one quoted and the PD extent at the same point is given beside it.

no_reaction.what: Sox9->Bmp and Sox9->Wnt couplings and the Bmp/Wnt->Sox9 terms all set to zero; diffusion, production and decay left in place.

no_initial_perturbation.what: full model, but the t=0 perturbation of S is omitted, so the field starts at the exact homogeneous steady state (verified analytically: S*=0, B*=alpha_B/k5, W*=alpha_W/k9 makes all three time derivatives vanish at every point, whatever the local Fgf level).
no_initial_perturbation.result: DID NOT STAY FLAT, and this is reported rather than quietly dropped.
no_initial_perturbation.interpretation: The state is linearly UNSTABLE with max growth rate 8.18 per model time unit, and the run is 60 time units long, so double-precision rounding at the 1e-16 level is amplified by roughly exp(490) and saturates long before the end. A linearly unstable state cannot be held flat numerically, so this arm cannot test what it was designed to test. What it DOES establish is the converse: the pattern is not an artifact of the injected noise, because it forms without any. The arm that genuinely tests flatness is no_reaction (which passed), and the sub-critical end of bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced, which is linearly stable and does stay flat.

per_step_noise.what: dt-scaled additive Gaussian noise on S at every step instead of a single t=0 perturbation (the published scheme is 1% multiplicative noise per step, which vanishes identically at S*=0).
per_step_noise.must_show: the same element counts as the default noise model

positive_and_negative_control_for_the_co.what: The counter is run against a case it must flag and a case it must not: the wild-type-like field (must return a multi-element count) and the no-reaction field (must return 0).

data.classification_rule: Applied to the Sox9 field S at t = T_end, on the masked domain. (1) AMPLITUDE GATE: if p99(S) - p1(S) < 0.05 model concentration units, or p99(S) <= 0, the field is called unpatterned, element_count = 0, class = 'none'. (2) THRESHOLD: Sox9-high = {S > 0.25 * p99(S)}. The homogeneous steady state is S* = 0 by construction, so this threshold is referenced to the known unpatterned baseline and the unpatterned background can never be counted as an element. (3) MINIMUM SIZE: connected components (4-connectivity) of the Sox9-high set with area >= 0.10 * lambda_elem^2 are counted as elements, where lambda_elem = lambda_meas_WT * lambda_lin(condition) / lambda_lin(WT): the wavelength MEASURED in the wild-type runs, carried to each condition by that condition's analytic linear-stability wavelength. It uses no measurement from the run being counted. (4) CLASS from the count n: n=0 -> 'none'; n=1 -> 'single element', or 'single fused domain' if that one component spans more than 70% of the anteroposterior width; 2<=n<=4 -> 'reduced'; n=5 -> 'normal digit number'; n>=6 -> 'increased (polydactyl-like)'.
data.classification_rule_change: The rule was declared before any sweep was run, and step (3) originally used lambda_lin(condition) itself rather than lambda_elem. It was CHANGED after the first full run, and the change is recorded here rather than quietly made. The reason is a defect in the specification, not a result I disliked: the linear-stability wavelength is about half the wavelength the saturated pattern actually has (measured, and reported under measured_wavelength), so a minimum area of 0.10 * lambda_lin^2 is four times too small and admits slivers at the anterior and posterior ends of the band as if they were elements. Every element count under the ORIGINAL rule is kept alongside, as element_counts_linear_rule in each sweep row and as sweeps_under_the_original_rule.wild_type. Under the original rule the wild-type count was [5, 7, 6, 5, 5, 4] (mean 5.33); under the revised rule it is [5, 4, 5, 4, 4, 3] (mean 4.17). The qualitative shape of every sweep is the same under both.

sweeps_under_the_original_rule.note: Per-condition counts under the original rule are in each sweep row as element_counts_linear_rule.

seeds.note: Turing patterns are seed-dependent. Every sweep point is run from 3 fixed seeds and the spread is reported as element_count_sd; the individual counts are kept in element_counts.

numerics.scheme: IMEX. Diffusion and linear decay of B and W implicit (one sparse LU factorisation per condition, reused every step); the cubic in S treated semi-implicitly as -S_new * S_old^2, which keeps S bounded; all couplings explicit. Zero-flux boundary on the masked domain.
numerics.deviation_from_published_numerics: onimaru2016 use an explicit Heun solver with dt = 0.002 on a triangular finite-volume mesh and a growing domain. This is a fixed cartesian grid, a static domain, and a semi-implicit solver.
numerics.dt_0.02_was_unstable: Measured: at dt = 0.02 the solution diverged to ~1e8; at dt = 0.01, 0.005 and 0.002 the final field agreed to 5 significant figures. dt = 0.01 is the default.

limitations: NO GROWTH. The real limb bud grows while it patterns, and raspopovic2014's and onimaru2016's simulations both run on growing meshes. On a static domain the elements form as condensations in a distal band rather than elongating into proximodistally running digit rays. This study measures element NUMBER, not element SHAPE, and the shapes here should not be read as digit morphology.
The five-element wild-type-like outcome is IMPOSED by the chosen paddle width, not predicted. Only the changes in element count across the sweeps are model predictions.

The mouse parameter set of raspopovic2014 was not obtainable. The numbers used come from onimaru2016's CATSHARK FIN simulation of the same network, and one of them (alpha_W) had to be changed to obtain a Turing instability at all.

All lengths are model length units. The model as published carries no physical length scale that I can verify, so no result here is in micrometres and no statement is made about the real size of any limb bud.
The linear-stability wavelength and the simulated wavelength differ by a factor of about two (see measured_wavelength). The simulated value is the one used for the critical domain size.

The classification into phenotype classes is a threshold rule on a simulated scalar field. It is objective and pre-declared, but 'normal digit number' here means 'five counted components in this simulation', not a mouse phenotype.
Only one noise model, one domain shape, and one gradient shape were explored. Turing element counts are sensitive to all three.

THE ASSUMED OPERATING POINT IS FRAGILE. Because the steady state was placed at S* = 0 by balancing k2*alpha_B/k5 against k3*alpha_W/k9, any parameter change that breaks that balance moves S* off zero and switches the cubic self-damping back on. A 20% change in alpha_W alone, or a 15% change in k2 alone, collapses the five-element pattern to a single fused domain (see the wnt_production_alphaW_scale and bmp_to_sox9_k2_alone sweeps). The bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced sweep exists because it changes the coupling WITHOUT breaking that balance, and it is the one to read for criticality. The fragility is a property of this reparameterisation, not a claim about the published model.

THE ELEMENT COUNT DEPENDS ON THE MINIMUM-SIZE CUT by about one element, because the anterior-most and posterior-most condensations sit where the paddle narrows and are genuinely smaller. The wild-type count is 5.3 +/- 0.9 under the original rule and 4.2 +/- 0.7 under the revised one, over the same six seeds, and the critical domain size moves by about a factor of two between them. Treat one element as the resolution of this measurement.
The grid-refinement arm changes the element count by 1 in two of three conditions, which is the same one-element resolution; the dt-refinement arm changes nothing.
what_this_does_not_establish: It does not establish that any real limbless or limb-reduced animal, or any real mutant, lacks limbs because of a change in a Turing wavelength or a sub-critical patterning system. No animal was measured here.
It does not establish that the BSW network is the correct mechanism of mouse digit patterning. That is raspopovic2014's claim, read here at abstract level only.
It does not reproduce any published figure. No comparison to published data was made, so no agreement with data is claimed.
A simulated phenotype class is not a phenotype.

sources.used_for: The equation form and every sourced numeric parameter below. This paper states in its own text that it uses 'the BSW model' of Raspopovic et al. 2014 (its reference 12) and that the Fgf gradient modulates the same parameters as in the mouse model, 'repressing k4 and boosting k7'. It also supplies the numerical recipe (Heun, dt=0.002, zero-flux, homogeneous steady-state initial condition, 1% Gaussian multiplicative noise per step) and the simple square-domain Fgf substitute exp(-3x) on 0<=x<=1.
sources.caveat: Onimaru et al. apply this parameter set to a GROWING catshark pectoral fin mesh, where Sox9 forms spots. It is the same network as the mouse model but not the mouse parameter set, which was not obtainable (see raspopovic2014).

data.runtime_note: runtime_seconds is for THIS invocation. When the figures are redrawn from the cached simulation results (--figures) it does not include the simulations. The cached results came from a full run of 179 simulations on 5 worker processes, 437.0 s of wall clock to the end of the sweeps on a shared 8-core host.

figures.alt: Simulated digit-like pattern in a limb-bud-shaped domain
figures.caption: Simulation. The pattern the model makes in a full-size paddle.

figures.alt: A strip of simulated patterns across the parameter sweep, from several elements down to none, each labelled with its element count
figures.caption: Simulation. One network, seven settings, three different knobs, all panels on one spatial scale. Mean element count over the seeds run at each setting falls 6.7 → 4.7 → 3.0 → 2.3 → 1.0 → 0 → 0, from more elements than wild type through reduced and single-element to none. The large number on each panel is the one seed drawn; the mean and its spread are printed beside it, because a Turing pattern is seed-dependent and the single panel is not the measurement.

figures.alt: Simulated element count against domain size, with the critical domain size marked
figures.caption: Simulation. Element count against the paddle's anteroposterior width, in units of the pattern's own measured wavelength. The field stops holding a complete element somewhere between about half a wavelength and about one and a quarter: 0.94 ± 0.10 under the counting rule used, 0.44 ± 0.05 under the rule declared first. The range is the honest answer, not either end of it.

figures.alt: Animation of the simulated BMP-SOX9-WNT pattern emerging in a limb-bud-shaped domain
figures.caption: Simulation. The pattern forming in the full-size paddle, from the seeded noise it starts in. No sound.
